items.title: About this demo
items.text:
This demo brings a retailer's sales, inventory, customer, marketing, fulfillment, and supply-chain data together in Microsoft Fabric. All records are synthetic, so demonstrations do not expose real customer or company data.

Historical sales and operations data lives in a Lakehouse and is presented through Power BI. Optional live events go to Eventhouse, where you can query them with KQL (Kusto Query Language).

Machine-learning outputs add forecasts and risk estimates. An ontology maps business relationships, and Data Agents answer natural-language questions over the deployed data.

items.title: Agentic application
items.text:
The optional local application places chat beside an embedded Power BI report. An orchestrator routes questions to Fabric data services or to operations agents that draft replenishment and retention proposals.

The Fabric data platform and the optional local application have different trust boundaries. The app can run synthetic replay, uses operator credentials for live calls, and delivers an embed token to the browser. Its approval store is local and its Eventhouse telemetry is best-effort, not durable production audit. Check the environment's readiness report before using live features. See decision boundaries.

For the underlying streaming, Lakehouse, Eventhouse, and semantic-model architecture, see Architecture overview.

items.title: What it is, and why it's useful
items.text:
The app uses the deployed retail-demo workspace to answer business questions and prepare local action drafts:

  • It routes metrics to the semantic model, named-entity relationships to the ontology, and supported live-sales questions to recent event data. A trace records the selected route and reason.
  • When a user requests an action, an operations agent reads the deployed synthetic data, applies business rules, and drafts a proposal for human review.
  • It attempts to send recommendations and approvals to Eventhouse. Ingestion failures can be suppressed, so verify delivery separately from the UI state.

The data platform uses one Fabric workspace; the local app, browser, identity, and router remain additional trust and cost boundaries. The same Gold tables feed the report, the agents, and the ML models. Eventhouse holds live sales and successfully delivered agent telemetry.

items.title: 1. The app surface: report + chat, side by side
items.text:
The app is a small FastAPI backend serving a single-page front end with three pages:

  • Dashboard places the Power BI report and chat side by side, using about 70% and 30% of the space. The report uses user-owns-data embedding: the backend obtains a Microsoft Entra ID token from the developer's az login session. The demo does not require a separate app registration or service principal.
  • Agent Operations refreshes an approval-funnel dashboard from Eventhouse agent_actions, with KPI cards, an events-per-minute timeline, a per-agent funnel, and a feed of ingested recommendations and approvals.
  • Ontology Explorer displays business entities and their relationships.

The orchestrator chooses the data source for a question.

items.title: 2. The orchestrator: which brain answers?
items.text:
An LLM intent router (gpt-4o-mini on Azure OpenAI, authenticated through Microsoft Entra ID) classifies each question into a route:

Route Goes to Example question Metric, ranking, trend, or ML rollup Data Agent over the semantic model "Top 10 stores by net sales, YoY %" Single named entity, in context Ontology MCP over the business graph "What segment and churn risk does loyalty member LC012304678 have?" Recent sales Live-sales shortcut over event data "Top products in the last 15 minutes" Decision or action Operations agent "Stock is low. What should we do?"

The live-sales shortcut currently uses a fixed 15-minute store-sales query. It does not guarantee the product grain or time window requested in a question. See the routing specification for gate order and fallback behavior.

To use Claude for routing, set RETAIL_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic and RETAIL_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The trace names the model used. If the LLM call fails, a deterministic keyword router selects the route. The Data Agent and ontology can fall back to each other when one cannot answer.

items.title: 3. The two MCP servers: Data Agent and Ontology
items.text:
The app calls both Fabric services through Model Context Protocol (MCP). Each call is a JSON-RPC POST to a streamable-HTTP endpoint, authenticated with a Fabric bearer token:

  • Data Agent MCP (.../dataagents/{id}/agent) answers aggregates, rankings, trends, and ML rollups over the semantic model. Fabric translates natural language into DAX and returns the answer without the generated query.
  • Ontology MCP (.../items/{id}/ontologyEndpoint) exposes the business graph. It connects a named entity's profile with related data, such as a customer's segment and churn prediction. Fabric translates the question into a graph query and returns rows with a natural-language summary.

Use named-entity graph lookups for relationships such as Customer → ChurnPrediction. Route broad aggregations and deep scans to the semantic model, and verify graph paths before presenting them.

You can connect to both MCP servers from VS Code. See the VS Code MCP setup for the .vscode/mcp.json setup.

items.title: 4. The operations agents: perceive, reason, recommend, log
items.text:
When a user requests an action, the orchestrator selects an agent that runs app-authored DAX. The trace can show these queries in full.

Inventory & Replenishment reads stockout-risk predictions, checks fact_reorders for SKUs without an open reorder, and joins dim_products for prices. It applies a 14-day inventory-cover rule and drafts reorders with Approve and Dismiss controls.

Customer Retention reads churn predictions, joins customer_segments for lifetime value, and selects a ranked campaign cohort. It adds cross-sell suggestions from the market-basket model and drafts a win-back campaign with Approve and Dismiss controls.

Both agents estimate a proposal's value and require human review. Local approval does not place an order or execute a campaign.

items.title: 5. The closed loop: write-back to the Eventhouse
items.text:
The app attempts to log drafts and approvals in Eventhouse agent_actions, alongside live sales events. Successfully ingested events feed the Agent Operations approval funnel and can be queried with KQL:

agent_actions
| where action_ts > ago(1h)
| summarize count() by bin(action_ts, 1m), action_status
| render timechart

Successfully ingested events are queryable inside Fabric. The source app/backend/eventhouse.py logs on daemon threads and suppresses failures; durable audit, authenticated per-user approvals, and production actions need the additional controls under THREAT-009 / SEC-012.

items.title: Under the hood: transparency and which model thinks
"Show me how the agent got the answer"
items.text:
The collapsible how I reached this trace below an answer records the source, router model, decision reason, and exact MCP tool call and arguments. For ontology results, it reconstructs an entity path from the returned columns and shows a row preview. For operations agents, it shows the app-authored DAX.

Fabric's Data Agent and Ontology services generate queries server-side and do not return the query text. Their traces show the request and returned evidence, not the hidden query.

items.title: Which model is doing the thinking?
items.text: The application controls the intent-routing model, which defaults to Azure OpenAI gpt-4o-mini and can be changed to Claude with an Anthropic key. Fabric controls the models that translate natural language into DAX and ontology queries. The application cannot replace those models.

items.title: Why this matters
items.text:
The application lets a presenter move from a report value to a question and then to a reviewable local proposal using the same retail data. Pricing, logistics, and marketing agents remain proposed extensions; see the decision experience specification.

For presentation steps, see the CIO walkthrough.

items.title: Local deployment state
items.text: Each workspace name determines a local environment key. Its ignored environment overlay, Terraform input, backend state, Terraform data directory, fabric-cicd configuration, live outputs, and run journal stay under that key. Generation configuration lives at utility/config/environments/<env>.yaml, rendered notebooks at utility/out/<env>/, and every publication phase stages under deploy/.generated/<env>/workspace/. Different environments do not share these local paths. Operators must still serialize runs for the same Fabric target; path isolation is not a distributed lock.

items.title: Current constraints
items.text:
• The default full-demo inventory includes live-preflight-validated preview features; explicitly selected core and standard inventories are preview-free.
  • Task-flow deployment uses metadata behavior outside a stable Fabric item source-control contract.
  • Offline validation does not prove live workspace readiness. The separate profile-aware verifier queries Fabric, Kusto, and Lakehouse SQL. Prior full-demo evidence does not validate later changes. Collect fresh required-path and optional-stream evidence for each environment and run.

See deployment requirements and the operations backlog.

items.text: setup-01 through setup-11 seed dictionaries, generate dimensions and facts, publish Silver, and build Gold directly in the Lakehouse. items.title: Optional live path
items.text:

Direct Lake is the Power BI connection mode that reads Lakehouse tables directly from OneLake without importing a second copy.

items.title: Identities
items.text:
• Python deploy-time operations use an Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell operator identity. Terraform uses Azure CLI or an explicitly configured provider-supported service-principal, OIDC, or managed-identity credential; it cannot consume an Azure PowerShell session.
  • KQL schema application runs from the local deploy process.
  • The streaming notebook uses its Fabric runtime identity and needs ingestion rights on the target KQL database.
  • Reports, KQL, ontology, and agents use assigned consumer permissions.

items.title: Data handling
items.text: All records are generated synthetic data for demonstration only. Production customer data is outside the supported boundary. Fabric workspace and item permissions control access; row-level privacy controls for generated records are not part of the default release.

items.title: Current controls
items.text:
• Local generation config and generated output are ignored.
  • Secrets are expected from identity, secret stores, environment variables, or ignored files.
  • KQL application is centralized.
  • Direct streaming requires pre-existing tables through FailIfNotExist.
  • Canonical public documentation is built only from reviewed docs/ content.
  • The default semantic model and agents may expose generated row-level detail to authorized workspace consumers.

items.title: Verification boundaries

items.text: Requirements define required outcomes, constraints, and acceptance criteria. Exact interfaces and workflows belong in specifications, current structure belongs in architecture, and risks and mitigations belong in security.

items.title: Traceability states
items.text:
Only these states are allowed:

State Meaning proposed Draft outcome that has not been accepted. accepted Normative outcome; implementation is absent or incomplete. implemented Exact implementation evidence exists; verification is incomplete. verified Exact implementation and verification evidence exist. blocked The outcome cannot progress until a named external or upstream gate is resolved. retired The outcome is no longer required and its replacement or rationale is recorded.

items.title: Module ownership
items.text:
Each module has one requirements page and one backlog. A backlog contains only:

  • ## Open
  • ## Settled — do not reopen

Keep completed work out of backlogs. Git history and traceability.md retain the evidence.

items.title: REQ-CORE-001 - Supported path
items.text:
The supported path shall use the Fabric-native retail-setup utility, setup notebooks, deployment framework, and Fabric source assets.

Acceptance: A new contributor can identify one supported entry point and no public guide presents a removed local generator as an alternative.

items.title: REQ-CORE-002 - Synthetic data handling
items.text:
The demo shall use synthetic data. Identity-like synthetic fields shall still be treated as sensitive when exposed through reports, models, ontologies, or agents.

Acceptance: Public guidance and access controls use the same classification.

items.title: REQ-CORE-003 - Reproducibility
items.text:
Historical generation shall be deterministic for a fixed configuration and seed, including distributed Spark execution.

Acceptance: Contract tests prove repeatable table schemas and representative values for the same seed.

items.title: REQ-CORE-004 - End-to-end outcome
items.text:
The supported deployment shall produce a usable Fabric workspace with the required Lakehouse, Eventhouse/KQL database, notebooks, pipelines, semantic model, report, and configured optional assets.

Acceptance: Post-deploy checks verify live workspace items and a minimal data flow. Local staging checks alone are insufficient.

items.title: REQ-CORE-005 - Truthful capability labels
items.text:
Documentation and demo scripts shall distinguish implemented, optional, manual, preview, and proposed capabilities.

Acceptance: Each presented scenario has a current source artifact, required setup step, and known limitation or backlog link.

items.title: REQ-AN-001 - Ordered KQL assets
items.text: KQL tables, ingestion mappings, functions, materialized views, and supporting objects shall remain ordered, repeatable, and executable as one database script.

items.title: REQ-AN-002 - Medallion layers
items.text: Live Eventhouse data and historical Lakehouse data shall feed typed Silver tables and documented Gold aggregates without ambiguous ownership.

items.title: REQ-AN-003 - KPI semantics
items.text: Every operational KPI shall state and implement its grain, time window, current-state rule, unit, and resolution behavior.

items.title: REQ-AN-004 - Deployable demo surfaces
items.text:
Querysets, dashboards, and rules shall be labeled as automated, manual, template-only, or proposed and shall use existing KQL objects.

See the Fabric analytics specification.

items.title: ENH-001 - Deploy Real-Time Intelligence dashboards and Activator scenarios as first-class assets
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / M
  • Outcome: Source-controlled Real-Time Intelligence (RTI) dashboards and deterministic Activator scenarios deploy with parameterized bindings. Activator is Fabric's event-driven alerting and action service.
  • Acceptance: Stockout, truck SLA, and pricing scenarios can be reset and triggered predictably from a selected profile.

items.text:
• Eventhouse stores recent events and runs KQL aggregations.
  • Lakehouse stores durable Silver/Gold history for Direct Lake consumption.
  • Materialized-view and function names must match all querysets, dashboards, and rules.

items.text: • Remote Terraform state coordination and serialization across pipelines and manual writers still need design and validation. Environment-local files and a pipeline's concurrency = 1 do not provide those controls.

items.title: IMP-001 - Verify alternate authentication and target selection
items.text:
• Priority / effort: P2 / M
  • Current boundary: Both credential modes receive the configured tenant. Orchestrated task-flow deployment uses the Terraform workspace, Lakehouse, Eventhouse, and KQL database IDs. Staged shortcuts, ontology, stream notebook, and queryset definitions receive the configured KQL database name, while configuration continues to reject a split Eventhouse/KQL topology.
  • Remaining outcome: Live Azure PowerShell and renamed-Eventhouse smoke runs must prove the locally contract-tested paths against Fabric.
  • Acceptance: Both credential types receive the configured tenant; task-flow deployment uses the resolved workspace ID; the effective KQL database name reaches staged artifacts; configuration rejects an unsupported Eventhouse/KQL-name split; request-contract tests cover bearer headers and non-default names and IDs; and Azure PowerShell plus renamed-Eventhouse smoke tests succeed. All local clauses are covered; the two live smoke clauses keep this item open.

items.title: IMP-012 - Introduce tiered deployment profiles and preview gating
items.text:
• Priority / effort: P2 / M
  • Current boundary: The shared manifest now resolves dependency-closed core, standard, and full-demo inventories. Configure, render, staging, Terraform, KQL, pipelines, Reporting, agents, task flow, dry-run output, and journals use that exact selection. Local and live preflight fail on blockers, source gaps, unsafe downgrades, disabled tenant switches, and unsuitable capacities before changing resources. Core is preview-free and excludes Reporting. Standard/full use an exact-run required ML gate and two-phase Reporting publication; their prior IMP-008 blockers are removed. Full-demo validates preview and capacity prerequisites through documented read-only Fabric APIs. A live full-demo run has proven tenant/capacity preflight, required Reporting, post-ontology publication, and fail-closed readiness.
  • Remaining outcome: Live runs must still prove core completion without previews and the standalone standard Reporting profile. Prior full-demo evidence is a baseline. Changes to isolation, resume, saved-plan safeguards, staging, and readiness need fresh integrated and live verification.
  • Acceptance: A tenant without previews can complete the default profile, while optional profiles fail preflight before partial publication. Exact local inventory, selection, live prerequisite, blocker, and ordering clauses have local implementations and tests. Fresh changed-path validation and the remaining core/standard profile proof keep this item open.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• retail-setup deploy is the supported orchestrator.
  • Each environment owns separate Terraform state, Terraform data, generated target inputs, generation settings, rendered notebooks, staged items (including post-ontology), bindings, outputs, and deployment journal.
  • Terraform provisions resources; fabric-cicd publishes supported items; KQL scripts remain ordered source.
  • The supported Eventhouse topology uses its automatically created default KQL database with the same display name.
  • Destructive reset assets are never part of an automatic normal run.
  • full-demo is the manifest default for every entry point. Reporting profiles publish the connected twins report and the native Operations Agent by default; core and standard are explicit reductions. Native Planning stays excluded unless explicitly included because it needs fixed credentials and starts non-cancellable billing.
  • Same-workspace pipeline notebook references use deterministic logical IDs and the default-workspace sentinel resolved natively by fabric-cicd, not generated per-notebook parameter rules.
  • fabric-cicd bulk publish stays opt-in while its upstream API is experimental and post-ontology Data Agent publication needs dynamic target-item resolution.

items.title: REQ-DEPLOY-001 - Environment boundary
items.text: Every deploy shall resolve one explicit workspace-derived environment and validate its tenant, workspace, resource identifiers, and isolated Terraform state before changing resources.

items.title: REQ-DEPLOY-002 - Ordered publication
items.text: Deployment shall provision required resources, stage and publish Fabric items, apply ordered KQL scripts, validate outputs, and start only the configured post-deploy work.

items.title: REQ-DEPLOY-003 - Authentication modes
items.text: Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell Python-client authentication modes shall target the configured tenant and pass real bearer credentials to every required Fabric API operation. Azure PowerShell session state shall never be presented as a Fabric Terraform provider credential. Apply/destroy shall require a provider-supported credential; otherwise deployment shall require validated outputs with --skip-terraform.

items.title: REQ-DEPLOY-004 - Honest result
items.text: A failed required step shall produce a failed or explicitly degraded final result. Optional steps shall be named and reported separately.

items.title: REQ-DEPLOY-005 - Profiles and previews
items.text:
The default profile shall be GA-safe and capacity-conscious. Heavy, preview, destructive, and manual demo assets shall require explicit selection and capability preflight.

See the deployment specification.

items.title: Open
items.text:
• Inspect the next Docs publication, gh-pages, /latest/, search index, and tagged versions for the corrected publication boundary (SEC-010). Local build success is not a live-site verification result.
  • Update the records with final generator-review and hosted/live evidence when available. Packaging/build and readiness code are complete locally; all five notebooks were rebuilt and drift checked. Do not keep completed implementation work open solely because external service validation remains outstanding.
  • The pinned generator's 404.html emits #__skip without a matching anchor. Source-document and navigation links pass; retain the theme-owned defect separately from content-link validation.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• Data Agent source .platform descriptions may be nonempty, agent-specific summaries. Other source artifact types retain exact manifest-description matching; staged items still receive the manifest-owned description.
  • Canonical site source is docs/; website/docs/ is retired.
  • Zensical replaces Docusaurus.
  • Generated site output is pushed to gh-pages.
  • Versioned documentation shows main as Latest plus the highest tagged patch revision for each SemVer minor line.
  • Backlogs contain only open work and settled decisions, never completed-work archives.
  • Dated implementation plans are removed after durable content is promoted.

items.title: REQ-DOCS-001 - Canonical source
items.text: docs/ shall be the only documentation site source. Root and component READMEs shall remain concise entry points that link to the authoritative pages. The site's entry pages shall offer role-based paths for business users, analysts, presenters, operators, and developers, plus a shared plain-language glossary.

items.title: REQ-DOCS-002 - Durable ownership
items.text: Requirements, specifications, architecture, security, guides, backlogs, and traceability shall have explicit owners. Dated plans and findings shall not remain systems of record.

items.title: REQ-DOCS-003 - Zensical site
items.text: The canonical Markdown shall build with the pinned Zensical version and generator-neutral links, navigation, Mermaid diagrams, and assets.

items.title: REQ-DOCS-004 - Reconciled claims
items.text: Commands, table counts, event counts, deployment inventory, schedules, semantic-model mode, optional features, and support status shall agree with the current repository. User-facing guides shall explain unavoidable technical terms on first use or link to the glossary, and shall distinguish required, optional, preview, manual, and proposed behavior in plain language.

items.title: REQ-PUBLISH-001 - Branch publishing
items.text: The documentation workflow shall build current content from docs/, build historical content from immutable SemVer tags, and push generated output to an orphan gh-pages branch without the Pages artifact deployment actions.

items.title: REQ-PUBLISH-002 - Version selector
items.text:
The published site shall show main as Latest and the highest stable SemVer patch revision for every tagged major.minor line. Release URLs shall remain stable at major.minor while selector labels show the selected major.minor.patch revision.

See the site specification.

items.title: ENH-009 - Deepen deterministic retail scenario realism
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / L
  • Outcome: Stable customer, vendor, lead-time, promotion, weather, and holiday states create visible, reproducible operational effects.
  • Acceptance: Scenario presets preserve determinism and move documented KPI targets in predictable directions.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• Generation is Spark-native and deterministic.
  • Lakehouse Delta tables replace local DuckDB/parquet as the active contract.
  • New data columns use snake_case; legacy TMDL-bound exceptions remain documented until migrated.
  • Shared business invariants are enforced by utility/src/retail_setup/generation/invariants.py: no sales while closed, no pre-launch sales, no same-day returns, product lifecycle dates present, and validated (non-degenerate) profile controls.

items.title: REQ-GEN-001 - Base table set
items.text: Historical generation shall create seven dimensions, nineteen fact tables, and ten Gold aggregates in the documented ag and au schemas.

items.title: REQ-GEN-002 - Authoritative contract
items.text: utility/src/retail_setup/generation/schemas.py shall own the generated Lakehouse table contract until a shared machine-readable manifest replaces it.

items.title: REQ-GEN-003 - Deterministic business behavior
items.text: The same seed and configuration shall produce deterministic dimensions, facts, lifecycle events, and Gold outputs.

items.title: REQ-GEN-004 - Business invariants
items.text:
Generated output shall satisfy referential, calendar, pricing, tax, promotion, inventory, return, and lifecycle invariants before publication.

See the data-contract specification.

items.title: Native availability acceptance - REQ-MLAI-006
items.text:
• Accept the stopped Operations Agent definition and generated playbook in the target tenant, including Teams destination and approved notebook action.
  • The base retail-availability-operations Agent is now published in retail-demo as item 40d42195-9488-4ca1-8ba7-a15fc29648e6, stopped, with its KQL source and instructions. Existing verified evidence includes 80 availability signals and the separate prepare-replenishment-case notebook.
  • Complete the UI acceptance: generate/review the playbook, verify the KQL source on the Build page, configure the Teams destination, and explicitly activate only after review. The publisher omits an empty playbook object because Fabric returned No rule definitions available in the playbook; the UI must generate it.
  • The public definition API returns HTTP 400 UnknownError for FabricJobAction, including Notebook and DataPipeline probes (d60c1ef9-fafc-4500-84d6-48f6d54d00d5, c4cc969c-eaee-410a-9e66-84ac1672ccaa, 28e32f8c-d4d4-45cc-96ab-aae5509160fb). Temporary probe items were deleted. The Fabric UI uses a separate OA workload endpoint. The publisher calls that endpoint, and live readback verifies one KQL source plus the prepare-replenishment-case Notebook action with CASE_ID.
  • Scripted playbook generation reaches the same UI endpoint but is not accepted yet. RetailOntology_AutoGen now contains the live StockoutRisk entity, store/product relationships, and required properties; the delegated Teams recipient is also configured. The generator still returns generic BehaviorModelGenerationFailed, including for a simple established Product rule. Successful generation/review and activation therefore remain a Fabric service gate rather than missing repository modeling.
  • Live prerequisites remain satisfied: non-trial F64 West US 3, user identity, Copilot/Azure OpenAI settings, KQL database, and Item.ReadWrite.All. Service principals and managed identities are unsupported; the tenant settings index lists no separate creation toggle.
  • Keep native Planning excluded under fixed-credential policy and leave SSO unchanged; operations-only deployment and human review do not require those Planning connections. Native Plan acceptance applies only to environments whose policies permit its documented prerequisites.
  • Configure and accept native approvals/SQL writeback in-product before any simulated execution bridge is added. Real ERP execution is outside scope.

items.title: ENH-003 - Ground semantic-model agents and gate ontology agents
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / M
  • Outcome: Agents have business descriptions, synonyms, safe-use instructions, approved questions, and capability-aware rebinding.
  • Remaining validation: Re-test named-entity and multi-hop ontology questions with explicit property names and decomposition guidance. Older raw response logs are not current proof: empty filtered joins, translation errors, latency, and Eventhouse-bound aggregation need fresh checks. Prefer semantic-model aggregation and bounded graph lookups.

items.title: ENH-004 - Prepare the semantic model for richer Copilot experiences
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / M
  • Outcome: Verified answers, AI instructions, narratives, and anomaly explanations are published only after KPI, ML, and governance gates pass.

items.title: ENH-007 - Add trustworthy ML lineage and explainability
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / L
  • Outcome: Every prediction includes model lineage, intended-use limits, feature evidence, calibration, and prediction-versus-outcome diagnostics.
  • Quality check: Validate market-basket coverage and diversity as well as nonempty output. Bounded product selection can concentrate rules.

items.title: ENH-010 - Migrate the ontology to the new TMDL experience
items.text:
• Priority / effort: High / L
  • Deadline: The old ontology experience retires on Jan 31, 2027. The UI can no longer create it; only the APIs can.
  • Current state: fabric/lakehouse/30-create-ontology.ipynb publishes the old entity-type JSON definition (EntityTypes/.../definition.json). It relies on an automatically derived graph and on the Digital Operations authoring API for field descriptions.
  • Outcome: RetailOntology_AutoGen is published in the new TMDL definition format, preserves the current entities, relationships, keys, and Eventhouse time-series bindings, and carries descriptions natively. It surfaces retail_model DAX measures as ontology metrics where Fabric allows this in automation. Data Agent, task flow, readiness, and app consumers keep working.
  • Known constraints: Semantic-model measures surface only as projected metrics, which TMDL cannot yet express. The new experience does not materialize a graph by default, and every ontology read, including MCP calls, is billed as Ontology Discovery. See the ontology definition reference.
  • Progress: The TMDL generator and the staged-cutover publisher (deploy/scripts/_ontology_model.py, deploy_ontology.py) are implemented with offline tests and run as the non-required publish-ontology-tmdl deploy step. Remaining work:
  • live acceptance, which needs a sign-in to the demo tenant, covering:
    • whether the service accepts Eventhouse time series bound through cusn shortcuts;
    • whether it accepts inactive relationships used as additional backing tables;
    • whether it accepts the dim_trucks.DCID (double) to ID (int64) relationship;
    • whether fabric-cicd can publish ontology items;
    • whether the MCP tools still work on the new item;
  • retiring the 30-create-ontology notebook once the TMDL path is proven (it is already skipped for TMDL-format items);
  • re-exporting the ontology Data Agent snapshots;
  • pointing app/backend/ontology_graph.py at the generator.

items.title: ENH-011 - Add ontology business rules
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Medium / S
  • Depends on: ENH-010. Rules exist only in the new experience.
  • Outcome: Natural-language rules for pricing constraints, stockout status, return windows, and replenishment policy are published in rules/*.tmdl. Every statement comes from the source that enforces it, and each rule links to the entities and properties it governs. Agents can retrieve them through the ontology MCP list_ontology_rules tool.
  • Boundary: Rules are guidance only; ontology does not execute them. The new experience has no Activator integration, so fabric/rules/ remains separate.
  • Progress: Nine source-checked rules are generated into the ENH-010 definition (deploy/scripts/_ontology_rules.py). Live acceptance is pending: list_ontology_rules must return every rule.

items.title: ENH-012 - Publish Data Agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Medium / S
  • Outcome: A documented manual post-deploy step publishes the semantic-model Data Agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot (Agent Store) and adds co-publishers. publish_info.json descriptions are written as orchestrator guidance, because the publish description becomes description_for_model.
  • Prerequisites: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, Copilot extensibility enabled for the account, and the tenant settings for cross-geo processing and consuming Data Agents from non-Fabric services. Responses may then leave the Fabric compliance boundary.
  • Boundary: No public API automates this publication. Copilot Studio tool integration is an optional alternative, not a replacement. See Consume a Data Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

items.title: Decision experience acceptance: REQ-MLAI-005
items.text:
• A Fabric Apps spike in app/fabric-app stores proposals and append-only reviewer decisions in a Fabric SQL database. It uses Fabric SSO identities, and DAB grants only read and create, with creates bound to the caller. Separation of duties and the decision timestamp are still enforced only in the client. Reporting profiles deploy it through the non-required deploy-fabric-app step, which needs Node.js 20+. Live deployment and the negative API checks are pending: see context/plans/2026-10-07-fabcon-live-tests.md.
  • Validate the living scenario and action contract end to end; do not infer completion from app/backend/replay.py.
  • Retain replay/live parity, golden answers, scenario generation/checksums, certified-grain reasoning, override/recalculation, package export, presenter reset, and synthetic-content scan as acceptance work.
  • Additional pricing, operations, logistics, merchandising, and composed per-store agents remain proposals. Hosted delegated identity, external action adapters, and Fabric Workload packaging require separate approval.
  • Preserve draft-only execution and the explicit audit/identity limitations under THREAT-009 / SEC-012.

items.title: IMP-008 - Align the active report with a trustworthy ML contract
items.text:
• Resolution: All 14 outputs have executable contracts and isolated tiers. The required validator and exact-run gate fail closed before Reporting. Historical baseline evidence recorded a full-demo deployment with more than 540 days of history through setup, required ML, optional ML, experimental ML, SQL metadata synchronization, semantic-model publication, and report validation. This settled tier/publication design is not fresh verification of current batch, generator, model, or readiness changes.

  • ML outputs are not assumed to exist in a core deployment.

  • Ontology and other preview-dependent automation require capability preflight.
  • Semantic-model agents and ontology agents have separate support boundaries.

items.title: REQ-MLAI-001 - Explicit support tier
items.text: Every ML, ontology, and agent feature shall be classified as required, optional, experimental, preview, or manual.

items.title: REQ-MLAI-002 - Trustworthy model output
items.text: Promoted predictive output shall have forward-looking methodology, stable grain, schema, model/run identifiers, as-of time, intended-use limits, and verification evidence.

items.title: REQ-MLAI-003 - Ontology binding
items.text: The ontology shall represent business entities and relationships. Eventhouse tables shall bind as time-series context on those entities rather than become duplicate event entities.

items.title: REQ-MLAI-004 - Governed agents (retired)
items.text:
Mandatory owner, persona, approved-question, prohibited-detail, and fallback metadata are outside the default demo release. Persona-specific agent experiences remain optional under ENH-003.

See the model-contract specification.

items.title: REQ-MLAI-005 - Evidence-bound decision experience (proposed)
items.text: A proposed decision experience shall distinguish live and synthetic replay, preserve certified grains and evidence, support human review/override, and emit draft-only action packages. It shall not imply production execution, guaranteed audit delivery, or verified financial outcomes. Acceptance requires the complete scenario and failure paths, not merely the presence of UI or replay code. See the decision experience.

items.title: REQ-MLAI-006 - Native availability decisions
items.text: An Operations Agent and optional native Plan shall use explicit source evidence for bounded replenishment planning. Reporting deployments shall publish the Operations Agent by default; a service rejection of the agent shall be reported as a warning without failing the rest of the deployment. Native Planning shall remain excluded unless explicitly included. Deployment shall publish monitoring stopped. Draft preparation shall require human approval; real purchasing and changes to historical data are prohibited. Native Planning shall require a supported shared model connection and explicit billing acknowledgement. Source publication, interactive feature acceptance, and external execution shall remain distinct claims; unresolved tenant/connection prerequisites shall fail honestly.

items.title: IMP-013 - Prove runtime readiness and publish freshness lineage
items.text:
• Priority / effort: P2 / L
  • Outcome: Post-publish tests and a single operator view establish live workspace usability and data freshness.
  • Acceptance: A successful deployment validates required items, bindings, KQL objects, schedules, pipeline execution, and freshness signals.
  • Implemented locally: retail-setup verify and deploy/scripts/verify_readiness.py provide the fixed profile-aware check taxonomy, read-only default, explicit exact-run pipeline option, redacted atomic report, and deployment-journal integration. Pagination, definitions, task flow, KQL sets, schedules, job states, freshness, aggregation, redaction, CLI, and journal behavior have unit/contract coverage.
  • Bounded consistency implementation: freshness.watermarks now includes deploy/scripts/data_consistency.py receipt/inventory key anti-joins, recent null-balance/orphan checks, and settled Gold sales reconciliation. Missing/empty samples are unknown; observed mismatches fail the optional check. Equivalent SQLite SQL and adapter/runner tests are local evidence, not universal all-table/full-history proof or executed Fabric SQL.
  • Historical baseline: A prior full-demo workspace exercised required items, definitions and bindings, exact setup/ML runs, Lakehouse SQL access, Reporting, ontology, Data Agents, and task flow. SQL endpoint metadata was synchronized for every returned table.
  • Remaining live validation: Revalidate the current changes' required readiness, cleanup-warning aggregation, batch/ML/Reporting, ontology, agents, and task flow. Prior live runs do not validate these changes. Execute the consistency SQL against the live Fabric SQL endpoint. Also start a bounded stream-events run and retain recent Silver watermark, Eventhouse ingestion, and checkpoint-identity evidence. These three checks are optional because streaming is intentionally manual; they are not the only current verification gates.
  • Local runtime boundary: Actual inventory, delivery as-of, and truck lifecycle expressions passed on local Windows; the Windows CI job now includes those three non-filesystem Spark tests. Full Spark/Parquet/E2E coverage remains on Linux; Windows filesystem support is not implemented. Changes to hosted CI, live Delta MERGE, and Fabric failure/recovery still require separate proof.

items.title: ENH-008 - Use more platform-native monitoring and governance
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / M
  • Outcome: Fabric workspace/Eventhouse monitoring, Monitoring Hub, governance, catalog, labels, and Purview/DLP touchpoints are part of the operator workflow.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• Prefer Fabric-native monitoring where it provides the required signal.
  • Run history and failures are evidence, not disposable console output.
  • Active-path tests use discovery and fixture-driven markers. Spark tests run in bounded process-isolated shards, while Windows, E2E, documentation, notebook drift, and repository contracts feed one required release gate.
  • Destructive recovery must validate the live target and preserve audit context.
  • Required deployment steps, task-flow publication, setup, and the exact-run required ML gate fail the deploy and persist an atomic run journal.
  • Setup-10 is the single Silver publication boundary; historical Silver and Gold candidates stage and validate before promotion, with compensating Delta restore/drop rollback on partial failure.
  • Streaming Gold stages all ten outputs before promotion and restores prior Delta versions if an attempted promotion fails.

items.title: REQ-OPS-001 - Live readiness
items.text: A successful deploy shall verify required workspace items, bindings, KQL objects, schedules, task-flow references, and a minimal executable data path.

items.title: REQ-OPS-002 - Unified freshness
items.text: Operators shall have one view of setup runs, streaming progress, pipeline status, ingestion freshness, model versions, and alert backlog.

items.title: REQ-OPS-003 - Safe recovery
items.text: Reset, destroy, recreate, replay, and manual fallback procedures shall state scope, prerequisites, preserved evidence, and confirmation gates.

items.title: REQ-OPS-004 - Supported-path CI
items.text:
CI shall give the active utility, deployment scripts, contracts, notebooks, KQL consumers, docs, and supported platforms equal or stronger coverage than retired paths.

See the operations runbook.

items.title: REQ-OPS-005 - Connected SSO operational twins
items.text:
The optional demo shall expose connected Store, Warehouse/DC, and Truck views grounded in recorded entity/shipment/SKU relationships. It shall preserve signed-in-user authorization, expose source time and uncertainty, and distinguish read-only what-if values from observed state. It shall not depend on fixed credentials or claim unsupported geometry, telemetry, reservations, or execution. Deployment shall be independently selectable and retain verifiable artifact, binding, and data evidence.

See connected twins.

items.title: ENH-002 - Make dynamic pricing the flagship closed-loop action story
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / L
  • Outcome: Governed approve/reject writeback, current recommendation state, observed impact, and audit history form one reusable action pattern.

items.title: ENH-006 - Improve usability, accessibility, and localization
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / M
  • Outcome: The report has latest-period defaults, drillthrough controls, alt text, keyboard and mobile support, readable contrast, appropriate culture and currency settings, and visible forecast confidence.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• The active semantic model is Direct Lake, not a documented KQL/Lakehouse hybrid.
  • Curated explicit measures are preferred over implicit aggregation.
  • Current-state and time-slice KPIs use overwrite snapshots, producer-aligned labels, dim_date slicing, volume-weighted rollups, and hidden non-aggregatable technical fields.
  • Optional ML tables require explicit support and deployment status.

items.title: REQ-BI-001 - Direct Lake model
items.text: The active semantic model shall use Direct Lake over the deployed Lakehouse contract unless a separately documented table intentionally uses another mode.

items.title: REQ-BI-002 - Governed model surface
items.text: Business measures, relationships, hierarchies, formats, and visibility shall be explicit. Technical keys and helper columns shall not appear as accidental business measures.

items.title: REQ-BI-003 - Optional predictive tables
items.text: Report pages that depend on optional predictive output shall be gated or show an honest empty state until the required notebook output exists.

items.title: REQ-BI-004 - Usable report
items.text:
The report shall support its named personas with discoverable navigation, accessible labels, current date defaults, and clear empty/error states.

See the semantic-model specification.

items.title: Open
items.text:
• Repeat target/authentication and destructive recovery smoke checks after the current environment/resume/saved-plan changes (SEC-001, SEC-009, IMP-001); local code is not fresh Fabric proof.
  • Inspect published current and historical documentation plus search indexes after release (SEC-010, THREAT-008).
  • Before shared hosting or external actions, validate delegated identity, authorized approvals, durable audit delivery, replay labeling, evidence-bound actions, idempotency, and fan-out limits (SEC-012, THREAT-009). These proposed controls do not reopen retired row-level RLS or mandatory Data Agent persona requirements.
  • Add a regression test that the ontology notebook rejects non-HTTPS and non-allowlisted Fabric service hosts before sending Power BI or workload tokens (THREAT-002).

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• Row-level RLS, field masking, and mandatory agent-governance metadata for generated customer-like records are outside the default release scope. The demo uses synthetic data only and relies on Fabric workspace and item permissions for access control.
  • Secrets are supplied through identity, secret stores, environment variables, or ignored local files.
  • Workflow actions use reviewed commit SHAs and no workflow installs runtime plugin marketplaces; Python dependencies, Terraform providers, and downloaded bootstrap installers use committed locks or checksums.
  • Operating-system package managers and GitHub-hosted runner images remain external trust roots; project dependency changes are repository-reviewed.
  • Security guidance without implementation or verification remains accepted, not verified.

items.title: REQ-SEC-001 - Threat and control ownership
items.text: Security threats shall have stable THREAT-* IDs and map to stable SEC-* controls, implementation evidence, and verification evidence.

items.title: REQ-SEC-002 - Synthetic-but-sensitive classification (retired)
items.text: This requirement is retired. The supported demo uses generated synthetic data only; row-level classification and privacy controls for those records are not a release requirement.

items.title: REQ-SEC-003 - Credential safety
items.text: Credentials and tokens shall not be committed or embedded in generated output. Required clients shall send the real token only to the intended endpoint.

items.title: REQ-SEC-004 - Least-privilege consumers (retired)
items.text:
This requirement is retired. Standard Fabric workspace and item permissions remain the access boundary, but field-level restrictions, RLS, and mandatory agent-governance metadata are outside the default demo scope.

See the threat model and controls.

items.title: ENH-005 - Publish persona-led demo journeys, presets, and prompt packs
items.text:
• Priority / effort: Idea / M
  • Outcome: core, standard, and full-demo presets have known runtimes, expected assets, presenter controls, and persona-specific questions.
  • Acceptance: A presenter can choose a preset and reproduce its documented demonstration using the supplied setup steps.
  • Current boundary: Persona journeys and prompt packs are documented in the presenter guide. The deployment presets, measured runtimes, and preset-specific asset controls remain open.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• retail-setup is the supported setup path.
  • Historical range input is --months; explicit public --start-date/--end-date examples are retired.
  • Setup logs use linear plain output rather than a fixed-footer TUI.

items.title: REQ-SETUP-001 - Guided entry points
items.text: Windows users shall have a PowerShell entry point and macOS/Linux users shall have a shell entry point. Both shall invoke the same Python guided setup.

items.title: REQ-SETUP-002 - Explicit configuration
items.text: Configuration shall select an environment, tenant, workspace, capacity, Lakehouse, Eventhouse/KQL database, store profile, history length in months, store count, and deterministic seed.

items.title: REQ-SETUP-003 - Rendered notebooks
items.text: Rendering shall produce twelve environment-specific notebooks: setup notebooks 01 through 11 plus stream-events. Dictionary content shall be pinned to an explicit Git reference.

items.title: REQ-SETUP-004 - Observable execution
items.text:
Guided setup and deploy output shall be linear and copyable. It shall separate each step and command and report failures explicitly.

See the CLI specification.

items.title: IMP-005 - Enforce one live data contract across Eventhouse, Lakehouse, and Power BI
items.text:
• Priority / effort: P2 / L
  • Outcome: One manifest owns stable event/path metadata, keys, timestamps, targets, and downstream coverage while validation derives physical fields, types, and nullability from authoritative sources.
  • Acceptance: Fixture tests prove every payload-to-model path and document intentional streaming-only or historical-only exceptions.
  • Repository status: Complete. The manifest declares 18 emitted events, 19 paths (including derived attribution), and four owned exceptions. Validation derives physical fields/types/nullability from authoritative sources; eight scenarios and a 23-event fixture set cover the acceptance matrix.
  • Remaining live validation: Capture a Fabric staging run through Eventhouse, optional Silver/Gold projection, and Direct Lake. The non-mutating repository gate is python scripts/check_data_contracts.py.

items.title: Settled — do not reopen
items.text:
• Direct Eventhouse ingestion is the supported live architecture.
  • The removed Kafka/Eventstream custom-endpoint design is not a future default.
  • Event field names must be read from source schemas rather than inferred.
  • Marketing attribution uses deterministic last-touch within seven days, transported by the envelope correlation_id, with one purchase per journey.
  • Attributed revenue excludes tax; promotion discounts apply before tax and approved payment cents must equal purchase total cents.

items.title: REQ-STREAM-001 - Event set and envelope
items.text: The live driver shall emit the documented eighteen event types with one common envelope and typed event-specific payload.

items.title: REQ-STREAM-002 - Supported sinks
items.text: The supported live path shall write directly to Eventhouse KQL tables through the Spark Kusto connector. An explicitly selected Delta sink may be used for development or validation.

items.title: REQ-STREAM-003 - Cross-layer contract
items.text: Every live event shall have a documented mapping to Eventhouse and, where applicable, Silver, Gold, ontology, and Power BI consumers.

items.title: REQ-STREAM-004 - Replay-safe progress
items.text:
Required writes and transforms shall fail closed or retain replay evidence. Checkpoints and watermarks shall advance only after successful publication.

See the event-contract specification.

items.title: Minimum deployment baseline
items.text:
Before a shared or customer-facing demo:

  1. Confirm the signed-in tenant and target workspace.
  2. Review workspace and item roles.
  3. Confirm generated files contain no credentials or operator-specific secrets.
  4. Confirm the workspace contains generated synthetic demo data only.
  5. Confirm monitoring and failure notifications are available.
  6. Validate that reset and recreate actions target the intended environment.

items.title: Supply-chain lock maintenance
items.text:
Change the owning input (requirements-*.in, utility/pyproject.toml, or deploy/terraform/providers.tf) before regenerating its reviewed lock:

python -m pip install uv==0.11.29
python -m uv pip compile requirements-docs.in --universal --generate-hashes --output-file requirements-docs.txt
python -m uv pip compile requirements-test.in --universal --generate-hashes --output-file requirements-test.txt
python -m uv pip compile utility/pyproject.toml --extra deploy --universal --generate-hashes --output-file utility/requirements-deploy.txt
python -m uv pip compile utility/pyproject.toml --extra dev --extra deploy --universal --generate-hashes --output-file utility/requirements-ci.txt

After changing the Fabric provider version, regenerate all supported platform checksums:

terraform -chdir=deploy/terraform providers lock `
  -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64 `
  -platform=windows_amd64 -platform=windows_arm64 `
  -platform=darwin_amd64 -platform=darwin_arm64

items.title: Threat model
items.text: This document records the demo's security threats. See controls.md for mitigations and traceability for implementation and verification evidence.

items.title: Scope and assumptions
items.text:
• Microsoft Entra ID is the identity plane for Fabric access.
  • Operators use Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell for Python clients; Terraform requires a provider-supported identity.
  • GitHub Actions builds documentation and can run privileged automation.
  • Supported records are generated synthetic data. Production customer data is outside the demo boundary.
  • Preview Fabric features are not available in every tenant.
  • Generated configuration and output are not durable sources of truth.
  • The optional local app is a separate operator/browser boundary, not a hosted multi-user service secured solely by Fabric permissions. Live embedding sends an operator-derived Power BI token to the browser. Replay is not live query evidence.

items.title: Assets
items.text:
• Workspace roles, item permissions, and resource bindings.
  • Lakehouse, Eventhouse, semantic-model, ontology, and Data Agent access.
  • Deployment credentials, tokens, and environment-specific identifiers.
  • Run-history, freshness, approval, and verification evidence.
  • Canonical documentation and the public static site.

items.title: Specifications
items.text:
Specifications define exact behavior: interfaces, files, schemas, mappings, workflow order, state transitions, errors, compatibility, and current known divergence.

Requirements describe what must be true. Architecture describes where components sit. Security describes threats and controls. The guides turn these specifications into procedures.

Follow this setup sequence:

Location Ownership deploy/config/deploy.yml Shared deployment defaults deploy/config/environments/<env>.yml Ignored workspace target overlay utility/config/environments/<env>.yaml Ignored environment-specific generation configuration; legacy utility/config.yaml is a read fallback utility/out/<env>/ Environment-specific rendered notebooks deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform.tfvars Ignored Terraform input deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform.tfstate Ignored isolated Terraform state deploy/.generated/<env>/fabric-cicd/ Ignored publication config and rewrites deploy/.generated/<env>/ Ignored live outputs, run journal, and combined KQL deploy/.generated/<env>/workspace/ Environment-specific Fabric item staging

items.title: Time and determinism
items.text:
• Use UTC timestamps with timezone-aware APIs.
  • Historical configuration is centered on months; the derived range ends yesterday.
  • Seeded generation uses deterministic hash-based draws suitable for Spark.
  • Event timestamps must preserve lifecycle order even when ingestion can be out of order.

items.title: Naming
items.text:
• New pipeline columns use snake_case.
  • KQL event tables use snake_case.
  • Presentation names may be user-friendly.
  • The current physical contract still contains PascalCase and mixed-case columns required by existing Tabular Model Definition Language (TMDL) bindings in the Power BI model. Those exceptions are explicit in schemas.py; documentation must not claim the current model is pure snake_case.

items.text: Tier Meaning Core Required for the supported historical demo Optional Supported only when explicitly selected and prepared Preview Requires tenant capability preflight and explicit consent Manual Source or template exists, but publication/configuration is not automated Proposed Backlog idea with no supported implementation claim

items.title: Documentation ownership
items.text: docs/ is the only site source. Requirements, specifications, architecture, security, and guides must link rather than duplicate normative content.

items.title: Purpose
items.text:
contracts/retail-demo.json defines shared metadata across the demo's modules. Its top-level sections are frozen at version 1.4.0:

  • metadata and version;
  • prerequisites and commands;
  • assets;
  • profiles;
  • readiness_expectations;
  • data_contracts, event_paths, and exceptions;
  • ml_contracts;
  • source_owners.

The resolver uses profile entries to select existing logical assets, notebook groups, pipeline folders, and Eventhouse KQL objects. Repository validation compares ML contract entries with producer notebook declarations, required runtime-validator declarations, and active TMDL projections.

items.title: Authority boundary
items.text:
The manifest defines stable IDs, logical ownership, support status, descriptions, source pointers, profile-to-existing-group/asset selection, dependency metadata, contract and path declarations, and explicit exceptions. It does not own item definitions or pipeline bodies. ML schema declarations are validated projections of their physical producer/TMDL sources, not a second unchecked physical schema.

Physical fact Authoritative source Available item types, notebook groups, and physical staging behavior deploy/config/deploy.yml and deploy/scripts/build_artifacts.py Event tables, fields, types, and JSON paths KQL DDL/mappings and driver-05-stream.py ENVELOPE/EVENT_PAYLOADS Historical Lakehouse tables, fields, and types utility/src/retail_setup/generation/schemas.py TABLES Active semantic-model tables and Direct Lake bindings model.tmdl references plus each table TMDL's executable schemaName/entityName partition ML output schemas Producer notebook ML_OUTPUT_CONTRACTS; active TMDL for the six Reporting outputs

Each physical inventory declaration specifies how to derive its members and which source to read. Validators calculate the inventory from that source. Do not copy item names, event fields, or table schemas into the manifest.

The live event extension follows the same boundary. The manifest stores the stable envelope/event/path IDs, business and dedupe keys, UTC event-time semantics, physical targets, terminal coverage, and named exceptions. Parsers derive fields, types, nullability, JSON paths, transforms, Gold outputs, and active TMDL bindings from the physical sources during every check.

Each event path must declare its own exact Silver, optional Gold, and optional semantic-model source pointers. Validation does not pool pointers across paths. The path mode, source/target asset roles, controlling contract IDs, and named terminal exception must agree with that path. The envelope declaration must select the ENVELOPE symbol owned by the event contract and share the physical driver source used for EVENT_PAYLOADS.

Every source pointer must resolve inside the repository. Validators parse selector-backed pointers using the declared selector. A pointer to a whole file or directory proves only that it exists and has an owner; it does not validate its contents. Contract checks use the declared selectors directly.

items.title: Readers and validation
items.text:
retail_setup.contracts provides the strict Pydantic loader and repository-aware validators. Validation checks:

  • the frozen schema, globally unique IDs, and internal references;
  • repository-local source existence and selectors;
  • profile references against existing artifact groups and pipelines;
  • profile dependency closure, deployment classification, group/asset agreement, exact item/KQL selection, staged counts, and workspace folders;
  • source .platform and staged item descriptions against manifest-owned asset descriptions;
  • source-derived inventory relationships;
  • Eventhouse DDL, ingestion mappings, and direct-writer field/type/path agreement;
  • all 18 emitted-event routes, the nine-field envelope, the operational unknown_event table, Silver/Gold transforms, and active semantic terminals;
  • each path's mode, asset/contract ownership, exact per-path sources, and semantic-or-exception terminal coverage;
  • the derived five-input marketing-attribution route;
  • every active TMDL table's executable Direct Lake binding, its agreement with sourceLineageTag, and the expected ag or au physical table;
  • representative wire fixtures, including nullable and unknown-event cases;
  • all 14 ML producer/source/schema/grain/temporal/lineage declarations;
  • required ML agreement across producer, validator, and active TMDL;
  • all 26 readiness check IDs, categories, profile applicability, and required/optional behavior against the unchanged runtime taxonomy;
  • declared inventory exceptions.

Run this read-only check from a repository checkout:

python scripts/check_data_contracts.py

It prints stable counts and source-derived streaming-only, historical-only, and operational boundaries. It never rewrites KQL, notebooks, schemas, or TMDL.

scripts/solution_manifest.py uses only the Python standard library. It exposes identity, prerequisites, canonical command examples, profile names and the default, publication counts/folders, manifest version, and a deterministic semantic SHA-256. Bootstrap reads it before installing dependencies; scripts/setup.py derives its --profile default from this view. Both readers reject primitive type coercion. Agreement and negative tests keep the projection aligned with the typed reader. Dry-run output, deploy journals, artifact inventories, and readiness reports carry the same manifest version/hash and resolved profile boundaries.

For the readable inventory, see the workspace and profile inventory.

items.text:
Later work should populate existing sections rather than introduce parallel manifests:

  • profile execution belongs in profiles; separate live core/standard proof remains under IMP-012;
  • ML methodology and outputs belong in executable ml_contracts; the live required-ML/Reporting gate was completed under the settled IMP-008;
  • event fixtures and routes are implemented in data_contracts, event_paths, and exceptions; live Fabric evidence remains IMP-005;
  • readiness taxonomy metadata belongs in readiness_expectations; actual live evidence remains environment-local and the manual-stream boundary remains IMP-013;
