Add a source-derived inventory when physical membership is needed. Add an exceptions record for intentional divergence and remove it when the sources converge.

items.title: Eventhouse/KQL scripts
items.text:
Deployment applies numbered scripts in repository order:

  1. 01-create-tables.kql
  2. 02-create-ingestion-mappings.kql
  3. 03-create-functions.kql
  4. 04-create-materialized-views.kql
  5. 06-ml-anomaly-detection.kql
  6. 07-pricing-approval-tables.kql

Each source file is a standalone, fail-fast .execute database script with (ThrowOnErrors=true) batch. apply_kql.py removes that one leading wrapper from each selected source and emits one flat outer fail-fast script; embedded or repeated wrappers are rejected.

items.title: KQL object inventory
items.text:
• 18 typed business event tables
  • unknown_event
  • anomaly_alerts
  • 3 pricing recommendation/decision tables
  • 5 core materialized views
  • 2 pricing decision metric materialized views
  • fn_pending_recommendations() for latest cross-event workflow state
  • functions for attribution, truck SLA, anomaly detection, and related queries

Core materialized-view definitions are time-independent; seven-day retention is applied as a materialized-view policy. Anomaly functions build explicitly bounded hourly series with zero-value defaults, then sort severity through a numeric rank while preserving the public result schema.

The direct live path writes typed tables and does not use the JSON ingestion mappings.

items.title: Lakehouse layers
items.text:
Layer Schema/location Role Live Bronze cusn shortcuts Read-only Eventhouse table references exposed to Spark; cusn is the demo schema used for these shortcuts Silver ag Typed dimensions, facts, and operational state Gold au Ten reporting aggregates and contract-tiered ML outputs

The primary historical path writes Silver/Gold directly through setup notebooks. The Eventhouse shortcut path is optional for incremental live projection.

items.title: ML output tiers and runtime validation
items.text:
contracts/retail-demo.json defines 14 executable output contracts. Each references its authoritative producer notebook and declares exact schema, grain, as-of and lineage fields, source tables, intended use, and limitations. The six required Reporting tables also reference their active TMDL projection. Repository validation fails when a producer, manifest declaration, validator, or TMDL projection disagrees.

The ML and AI contract lists all 14 outputs and their Required, Optional, or Experimental tiers.

15-validate-required-ml-contract runs after all required producers. It fails on missing or empty tables, incompatible schemas, null or duplicate grain keys, invalid probability/bound values, missing as-of or lineage values, and incomplete demand-forecast horizons. It does not create placeholder tables. Only its pipeline's terminal success permits Reporting publication.

items.title: Streaming-to-Silver behavior
items.text:
03-streaming-to-silver.ipynb reads Eventhouse shortcuts and replays a configurable interval from each per-source checkpoint in ag._watermarks. The default overlap is three hours to cover normal Eventhouse OneLake visibility latency. Once per day by default, a distinct per-source reconciliation checkpoint permits a bounded-cadence scan of older history. That scan anti-joins source dedupe keys against Silver and adds only missing rows to the same idempotent merge. Processing and reconciliation checkpoints advance only after the merge succeeds; null checkpoint timestamps still fail closed. Override the defaults with the REPLAY_OVERLAP_SECONDS and DEEP_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS notebook parameters or environment variables.

The pipeline passes Lakehouse/schema notebook parameters and uses concurrency = 1 to prevent overlapping runs of that pipeline. Manual notebook execution is not protected by that pipeline setting. The daily deep scan is cadence-gated, not a scan of all source history on every run.

Truck arrival/departure is handled as one lifecycle: Silver joins the two sources on truck, distribution center, store, and shipment before appending a completed fact_truck_moves row. It scans the retained truck sources and anti-joins completed Silver lifecycle keys so delayed counterparts are not lost behind a watermark. tests/test_truck_dwell_contract.py verifies the cross-layer source contract; live Fabric execution remains a separate gate.

Live-specific behavior and divergences:

  • inventory_updated deterministically continues prior balances, orders deltas by event time and trace ID, and repairs legacy null-balance suffixes for affected store/product keys;
  • picked and shipped events populate ag.fact_online_order_status;
  • fact_online_order_status is an owned streaming-only Silver contract: its exact schema and routes are declared in the Silver notebook, its terminal exception is validated from contracts/retail-demo.json, and 05-maintain-delta-tables.ipynb includes it and ag._watermarks in routine maintenance;
  • it is intentionally absent from schemas.py and the active semantic model because TABLES remains the historical contract;
  • live coverage is not equivalent for every historical fact.

Inventory also has runtime test coverage: utility/tests/generation/test_streaming_inventory_runtime.py executes the actual notebook transformation functions with real Spark DataFrames and windows. It covers prior-balance continuation, legacy-null repair, same-timestamp ordering by trace_id, and idempotent replay. The recorded local result is a pass on Spark 4.2 with a checksum-verified session-local JDK 17. Target-table lookup is stubbed; no live Delta MERGE, full Spark suite, or Fabric execution is proven by this test.

Watermark/replay behavior is fail-closed and contract-tested. The manifest declares all 18 emitted paths and derives the physical transform inventory from this notebook. python scripts/check_data_contracts.py fails if a route, terminal, mapping, key, or named boundary drifts.

items.title: Streaming-to-Gold behavior
items.text:
04-streaming-to-gold.ipynb writes each of the ten Gold candidates to a run-scoped staging schema. All ten must exist and pass row-count/schema validation before promotion. The notebook captures each prior Delta version; an attempted promotion failure restores pre-existing targets and drops newly created targets in reverse order. Rollback continues after individual restore errors and preserves staging when manual recovery is required.

Nine Gold tables have an emitted-event route. dc_inventory_position_current depends on historical-only fact_dc_inventory_txn and is therefore part of the named historical boundary. The derived attribution path combines five Silver inputs and terminates at fact_marketing_attribution and campaign_performance_daily in the active semantic model.

items.title: Querysets
items.text: Checked-in KQL files are bundled as one KQLQueryset item with one tab per query. Deployment rewrites its cluster/database binding.

items.title: Dashboards and rules
items.text: Dashboard JSON/templates and KQL rule definitions are source inputs, not guaranteed deployable items. They may require manual import and binding. Activator is Fabric's event-driven alerting and action service. Claims about five-minute schedules or deployed Activator actions are not current defaults.

items.title: KPI semantics
items.text: Current-state tables are overwrite snapshots. KQL and DAX use producer-aligned status labels, shared date slicing, source-correct grain, volume-weighted rollups, and hidden non-aggregatable technical fields. Repository contract tests guard those semantics.

items.title: Receipt repair utility
items.text: 90-augment-and-dedupe-receipts.ipynb materializes and validates candidates and backups before replacing receipt-grain targets. It records each attempted promotion before issuing the replacement statement. A server commit followed by a client exception therefore includes that target in reverse-order rollback, rather than silently restoring only earlier targets. tests/test_lakehouse_batch_ml_fixes.py exercises this failure window with executable mocks. Local batch work is complete; actual Fabric/Delta rollback execution remains a separate live gate.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text:
05-maintain-delta-tables.ipynb skips genuinely absent optional tables, including optional ML/streaming state; missing required historical tables fail its base-inventory check. Checks and maintenance statements use fully qualified configured Lakehouse/schema/table names. Only genuine table absence is skipped: permission, catalog, and other real AnalysisException failures propagate rather than being reclassified as optional absence. Operation failures fail the notebook. Deployment supplies configured Lakehouse/schema parameters to pipeline notebook activities.

These changes are implemented locally. Fresh remote KQL, Silver/Gold, pipeline-concurrency, and maintenance smoke tests remain release gates.

items.title: Current order
items.text:
The supported deploy orchestrator is retail-setup deploy.

flowchart LR
    Resolve[Resolve manifest profile]
    Preflight[Validate profile preflight]
    Config[Generate environment config]
    TF[Terraform init/apply or resolve existing outputs]
    StageInfra[Stage infrastructure without Reporting]
    PublishInfra[Publish infrastructure]
    KQL[Build and execute ordered KQL script]
    Setup[Wait for setup-pipeline]
    RequiredML[Wait for ml-required + validator]
    StageReporting[Stage Reporting]
    PublishReporting[Publish Reporting]
    ExtendedML[Run selected post-Reporting ML]
    RefreshSQL[Synchronize Lakehouse SQL endpoint metadata]
    Validate[Validate publication]
    Ontology[Create or validate ontology]
    Agents[Publish Data Agents]
    TaskFlow[Deploy and read back complete task flow]
    FinalVerify[Verify complete readiness]

    Resolve --> Preflight --> Config --> TF --> StageInfra --> PublishInfra --> KQL
    KQL --> Setup --> RequiredML --> StageReporting --> PublishReporting
    PublishReporting --> ExtendedML --> RefreshSQL --> Validate --> Ontology
    Ontology --> Agents --> TaskFlow --> FinalVerify

Local and live preflight run before Terraform destroy/apply, item publication, or KQL changes. Local preflight validates source and state contracts. The orchestrator invokes it with --source-only to check committed notebook inputs before rendering; it does not require a prior rendered output set. Explicit rendered-output validation resolves utility/out/<env>/, not the shared legacy output directory. Live preflight uses documented Fabric APIs to validate tenant switches and capacity state, size/tier (SKU), region, and Spark sizing.

Deployment passes --resume-capacity to live preflight. Its active-capacity fast path is read-only; paused capacity may be resumed through Azure Resource Manager after resolving the configured capacity name. An explicit workspace.capacity_resource_id bypasses discovery. Otherwise, the configured subscription is searched, or all accessible subscriptions owned by the configured tenant are enumerated. All pages and subscription ownership must be validated, and exactly one capacity name match must remain. An inaccessible page or subscription cannot be skipped to produce an apparently unique match. Only Microsoft.Fabric/capacities F-SKU resources in Paused or Suspended are resumed, with API version 2023-11-01. Identity/name/subscription mismatches, inactive trial/Premium capacities, and ambiguous Fabric lookup results fail before the resume request. Fabric Inactive alone is not proof of an ARM paused state.

Resume uses a separate ARM token for the configured tenant/authentication mode, submits at most one POST, honors asynchronous operation headers and Retry-After, and polls resource and Fabric states with a bounded wait. HTTP 429 GET responses honor Retry-After within that deadline, including discovery and operation polling. POST retries are not introduced by throttling. Lost POST responses and conflicts trigger state reads, not blind repeat mutations. Polling URLs must remain on the trusted HTTPS ARM host. Resuming restarts billing; no scale, assignment, creation, or later automatic pause is performed. Default wait is 600 seconds. Standalone live preflight without the flag, deploy dry runs, and readiness remain nonmutating. deploy --resume reexecutes live preflight even when the prior run recorded it as successful, while retaining completed setup/ML steps. Before publication, target-access validation also proves that captured workspace IDs match managed state and resolve to the configured live workspace for the deployment operator.

The CLI saves terraform.tfplan and validates its JSON resource changes before apply confirmation. Review that file with terraform show; the plan guard captures its subprocess output rather than displaying a human-readable diff. Apply consumes that exact saved plan with -auto-approve; it does not recalculate an unreviewed plan. Deletion or replacement of fabric_workspace, fabric_lakehouse, or fabric_eventhouse fails the normal plan guard. Intentional destructive changes require the explicit --recreate workflow, including its destroy confirmation.

items.title: Command modes
items.text:
Mode Exact behavior --dry-run Validates existing configuration and the Terraform/Python authentication boundary, then prints the plan without subprocess execution or live target access. With --skip-terraform, it also validates captured outputs. --yes Pre-confirms gated Terraform steps and existing-workspace handling; it never skips required pipeline gates. --skip-terraform Omits Terraform only after captured outputs match the selected environment, workspace, resource names, and non-placeholder IDs. --resume Reuses a compatible incomplete journal's contiguous SUCCEEDED prefix, then retries from the first other state. --recreate Runs destroy, polls Fabric until the workspace name is absent (bounded at 180 seconds), then applies and publishes.

--recreate and --skip-terraform are mutually exclusive. A normal interactive run detects an existing workspace by display name and offers update-in-place or recreate. --yes skips that prompt.

--resume cannot be combined with --dry-run or --recreate. The environment, targets, profile, manifest hash, ordered step IDs, and content/command fingerprint must match. The fingerprint covers deployment sources, selected configuration, dictionary files, and ordered commands. Legacy journals without the required plan/fingerprint fields are rejected; compatibility is never assumed. Failed, degraded, skipped, or pending steps do not extend the reusable prefix. Completed runs cannot be resumed. An interrupted recreate preserves its prior recreate target identity only when every prior step through deletion-wait succeeded. An unfinished destructive phase refuses automatic resume; explicit operator review and restart are required.

Pipeline gates persist one bounded evidence document immediately after a successful submission and before polling. The document contains only exact workspace/pipeline/run correlation, Location, status, and timestamps. A compatible RUNNING gate is resumed by polling that exact Location; the orchestrator never submits a replacement. Completed evidence is adopted, active evidence remains awaited, and terminal failure remains failure. Monitor timeout is a resumable local outcome and does not cancel or classify the remote Fabric run as failed. Ambiguous POST outcomes reconcile only one exact-pipeline run in the request window; zero or multiple candidates fail closed.

Before retrying a pending apply, resume regenerates and checks the saved plan. Before retrying a pending item-publication phase, it rebuilds that phase's staging, including post-ontology artifacts. A successful build record does not prove that temporary local files remain intact. Resume is not a substitute for live target validation or readiness evidence.

items.title: Workspace-scoped environments
items.text:
configure derives one environment key from the Fabric workspace name. It lowercases the name, converts punctuation and spaces to hyphens, and omits a leading retail-demo- prefix. For example, retail-demo-alice becomes alice.

Each key owns one ignored target overlay and one ignored generated directory. The overlay contains operator-specific tenant, capacity, workspace, and optional existing-item identifiers. The tracked deploy.yml contains shared defaults only. After Terraform, fabric-cicd targets the validated workspace ID rather than resolving a potentially duplicate display name.

items.title: Generated files
items.text:
Path Role Tracked deploy/config/environments/<env>.yml Workspace-specific target overlay No utility/config/environments/<env>.yaml Environment-specific generation settings; legacy utility/config.yaml is a read fallback No utility/out/<env>/ Rendered notebooks and render manifest No deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform.tfvars Terraform input rendered from merged YAML No deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform.tfplan Saved, guarded Terraform plan applied after confirmation No deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform.tfstate Local Terraform backend state No deploy/.generated/<env>/.terraform/ Terraform backend and provider data No deploy/.generated/<env>/fabric-cicd/config.yml Publication environment and item scope No deploy/.generated/<env>/fabric-cicd/parameter.yml Workspace, item, OneLake, KQL, and agent rewrites No deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform-output.json Captured live identifiers No deploy/.generated/<env>/database.kql Combined ordered KQL script No deploy/.generated/<env>/capacity-sizing.json Fresh, non-secret live capacity evidence and derived custom Spark pool bounds No deploy/.generated/<env>/deploy-run.json Atomic step/status journal for the latest deploy run No deploy/.generated/<env>/run-history/<hashed-run-id>.json Prior journal archived before a different new/resumed run replaces the latest journal No deploy/.generated/<env>/pipeline-evidence/<step-id>.json Bounded exact pipeline item/run/Location/status evidence used for reattachment No deploy/.generated/<env>/artifact-inventory-<phase>.json Validated manifest/profile/count/folder inventory for one publication phase No deploy/.generated/<env>/readiness-report.json Redacted profile-aware live evidence No deploy/.generated/<env>/workspace/ Staged Fabric items for every publication phase No

Terraform receives an environment-specific TF_DATA_DIR and local backend path. Parallel Terraform operations therefore cannot select or mutate another workspace's state. The orchestrator also isolates generation configuration, rendered output, and staging, including post-ontology staging, by environment. Do not run concurrent deploys against the same environment; different local paths are not a distributed lock on a shared Fabric target. Lower-level build helpers may retain legacy defaults, so use the orchestrator for isolation. The supported state path is a local backend; remote-backend coordination and distributed serialization across separate pipelines/manual writers remain external design and validation gates.

A legacy deploy/terraform/terraform.tfstate with no environment-local state fails preflight. The operator must verify its workspace ownership and move it to exactly one deploy/.generated/<env>/terraform.tfstate path.

If environment-local state exists, preflight reconciles its profile, resource, and target-output signals with terraform-output.json. Missing profile evidence, missing captures, or stale identities fail closed even when the state currently has no managed instances. A downgrade that would remove a profile-controlled Eventhouse or custom Spark pool requires explicit --recreate; absent evidence never authorizes deletion.

For custom-pool profiles, live preflight derives sizing from the resolved capacity SKU before Terraform configuration generation. Supported SKUs are F<n> and FTL<n>. Base Spark capacity is 2 vCores per CU; the framework reserves 25%, divides the remaining vCores across the root notebook producers in ml-required.DataPipeline, and uses 8-vCore Medium nodes. Per-session maximum nodes are floor(floor(CU * 2 * 0.75) / (producer_count * 8)), clamped to 2–16; the minimum is 2. A capacity that cannot provide a driver plus executor to every producer fails closed. Burst capacity is excluded from the calculation.

Config generation validates the evidence environment, configured capacity identity, SKU arithmetic, producer count, integer bounds, and deployment-run freshness. The journal stores the stable sizing identity. A resumed run regenerates and replans when sizing changes before apply; sizing drift after a successful apply requires a new plan and cannot be adopted by resume. Starter pool profiles do not require or consume capacity evidence.

items.title: Authentication boundary
items.text:
Azure CLI mode is shared by the Python clients and Fabric Terraform provider. The CLI tenant is validated before mutation, and Terraform receives an explicit tenant_id.

Azure PowerShell mode applies only to Python Fabric clients. Terraform apply/destroy is rejected before command execution unless exactly one provider-supported service-principal secret/certificate, OIDC, or managed-identity credential is configured. Otherwise the operator must use validated prior outputs with --skip-terraform. In this mode the provider's Azure CLI fallback is disabled, preventing an unrelated CLI context from being used silently; conflicting provider tenant variables are rejected.

items.title: Manifest authority and executable profiles
items.text:
contracts/retail-demo.json defines stable asset IDs/descriptions, support metadata, dependencies, profile-to-existing-asset/group selection, expected publication counts/folders, canonical commands/prerequisites, and readiness expectations. Physical item and schema definitions remain in deploy/config/deploy.yml, deploy/scripts/build_artifacts.py, and the source folders. Manifest source pointers are validated rather than used to duplicate physical schemas.

Resolution computes dependency closure and rejects unknown, cyclic, or unclassified selected assets. Pipeline selection is exact and independent of notebook references. All profiles exclude the destructive reset group.

Profile Assets Groups Pipelines KQL scripts Publication behavior core (explicit selection) 1 setup 0 0 Lakehouse shell and eleven rendered historical setup notebooks; no Eventhouse, Reporting, ML, stream, preview, task flow, or custom pool standard 8 setup, core, stream, ml-required 5 6 Supported real-time/streaming plus fail-closed required ML/Reporting path; starter pool and no preview features full-demo (manifest default for every entry point) 14 standard groups plus ml-optional, ml-experimental, ontology, utility 7 6 Required Reporting gate plus post-Reporting extended ML and advanced/preview features except reset

The exact initial infrastructure/Reporting counts are 5+0, 30+2, and 40+2 respectively. They and the workspace-folder sets are validated while staging; every staged .platform description is projected from the selected manifest asset. See the canonical workspace inventory. Checked-in Data Agent .platform files may retain nonempty agent-specific summaries distinguishing semantic-model and ontology scope. This source metadata exception does not change staging's manifest-description projection or exact description contracts for other artifact types. The prior IMP-008 profile blockers are removed because the required path is now executable and fail-closed. Full-demo checks Ontology/Data Agent tenant switches with the admin tenant-settings API and validates the selected capacity with the capacities API. Settings changes remain administrator-owned because Fabric publishes no tenant-settings update API.

The manifest marks full-demo as the default, so the guided wrappers, scripts/setup.py, and direct retail-setup commands all deploy it unless core or standard is selected explicitly. Configuration enables the connected twins report and the native Operations Agent by default for any Reporting profile; native Planning stays excluded unless include_plan is set. The operations-only publication step is non-required, so a Fabric rejection of the agent degrades the deployment instead of failing it.

No profile enables schedules or starts the live stream. The source daily-maintenance schedule remains present but disabled. Dashboard templates and rule definitions remain manual sources even though full-demo classifies them in its logical inventory.

items.title: Two-phase Reporting publication
items.text:
For standard and full-demo, the orchestrator:

  1. stages and publishes infrastructure, notebooks, experiments, and pipelines without the Reports and Semantic Models folders;
  2. waits for setup-pipeline to complete;
  3. starts ml-required; its six independent producers fan out concurrently, and the validator joins all six successful producer activities before the pipeline can complete;
  4. stages and publishes the semantic model and report only after status Completed;
  5. runs any selected optional/experimental pipelines after Reporting;
  6. synchronizes Lakehouse SQL endpoint metadata so newly written tables become visible to SQL and Power BI clients.

setup-pipeline, ml-required, ml-optional, and ml-experimental each declare concurrency: 1 to prevent overlapping duplicate runs. The six required-ML producer activities retain retry: 0. Only 15-validate-required-ml-contract has a bounded retry of two attempts at 120-second intervals and a one-hour timeout, so transient validation failures do not replay successful producers.

The required pipeline's final activity is 15-validate-required-ml-contract. A missing, empty, schema-incompatible, duplicate, invalid, or temporally incomplete required output fails the pipeline. Skipped, failed, cancelled, deduplicated, timed-out, or unknown run states all fail closed and leave Reporting unpublished. Optional and experimental failures mark the journal DEGRADED but do not retract required Reporting.

Phased Reporting profiles reject deployment.unpublish_skip: false. Unpublishing from a partial infrastructure or Reporting stage could otherwise delete healthy items absent from that stage. This setting is a configuration safety check, not permission to skip the required publication gates.

SQL endpoint metadata synchronization is also optional at the step level. A failure marks the journal DEGRADED; the later readiness check still fails closed if any required Reporting table is unavailable.

items.text:
The resolver derives item_types_in_scope from the selected assets:

  • core: Lakehouse, Notebook

items.title: Parameter rewrites
items.text:
Generated parameter.yml rules rewrite:

  • OneLake and Direct Lake source identifiers;
  • KQL database item IDs and query URIs;
  • semantic-model connection IDs where configured;
  • Data Agent workspace, semantic-model, and ontology item IDs.

Pipeline staging replaces same-workspace notebook references with each notebook's deterministic logical ID and the default-workspace sentinel. fabric-cicd resolves those values natively during publication, avoiding generated per-notebook parameter rules.

Bulk publish is not enabled by default. The upstream API remains experimental, and full-demo post-ontology publication still uses dynamic target-item resolution for Data Agents.

items.title: KQL application
items.text:
deploy/scripts/apply_kql.py concatenates only the ordered KQL files selected by the profile into one outer database-script payload and can execute it against the resolved KQL database with the Kusto Python SDK. Executing KQL without an environment/profile inventory is unsupported. Core selects no KQL.

The required target is the configured KQL database, not a hard-coded default. The current topology uses the default database created with the Eventhouse and therefore requires the same display name. Artifact staging rewrites only the known shortcut, ontology, stream, and queryset target names in generated copies. Both credential modes receive the configured tenant. Live Azure PowerShell and renamed-target verification are tracked by IMP-001.

items.title: Task flow and ontology timing
items.text:
The orchestrator supplies Terraform output to task-flow deployment, so the workspace, Lakehouse, Eventhouse, and KQL database bind by resolved ID. Published items not owned by Terraform still bind by type and display name. --workspace <name-or-id> remains an alternative target, but deployment still requires matching --environment and --profile full-demo; unscoped legacy task-flow deployment fails.

Ontology creation is separate from setup-pipeline and the required Reporting gate, but it completes automatically later in the same full-demo deploy. The orchestrator starts the deployed 30-create-ontology notebook on every full-demo deployment. The notebook updates an existing ontology in place or creates it when absent, requires the derived-graph definition rebuild to succeed, and then the orchestrator waits for both terminal notebook success and exactly one stable ontology item.

The next phase publishes both Data Agents and deploys the source-controlled task flow. Before mutation, source coverage must include every selected full-demo artifact. After mutation, the metadata service is read back and all 14 tasks, 60 item bindings, and 14 edges must match exactly.

The recovery command reruns the same idempotent phase:

retail-setup post-ontology --env <env>

This command creates the ontology when absent, rejects duplicate ontology items, stages and publishes Data Agents, deploys and reads back the task flow, and runs complete readiness verification.

Task-flow deployment fails before publication when any selected reference is unresolved; it never publishes a silently partial graph. Normal full-demo deployment and the recovery command use the same completion path.

Task-flow publication currently relies on Fabric/Power BI metadata behavior that is not a stable public source-control item contract.

items.title: Failure semantics
items.text:
• Required initial plan and ontology/task-flow completion commands fail their respective run.
  • Blockers, missing selected sources, invalid pipeline references, disabled tenant switches, unsuitable capacities, and unsafe profile downgrades fail before mutation.
  • For gated profiles, setup and required ML are mandatory exact-run terminal gates. --yes suppresses prompts but never skips either gate.
  • Post-Reporting optional/experimental ML failures are recorded and execution continues.
  • The orchestrator executes an explicit dependency graph with separate resource limits: one Spark-heavy step and up to four non-Spark/API steps by default. Required failures prevent descendants from starting; optional failures do not cancel independent siblings. Final task-flow publication, folder reconciliation, and readiness wait for every selected branch to become terminal.
  • SQL endpoint metadata synchronization failures are recorded as optional degradation. Required-table visibility is checked again by readiness.
  • Recreate polls every visible Fabric workspace page and fails closed on timeout or malformed pagination before Terraform apply.
  • deploy-run.json records PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, DEGRADED, SKIPPED, and FAILED step states plus overall RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, DEGRADED, or FAILED. It stores no raw command output, environment variables, tokens, or tenant identifiers and redacts credential-like exception text.
  • Before a new or resumed run replaces the latest journal, the prior journal is atomically archived under run-history/, using the SHA-256 hash of its run ID as the filename. Latest-journal replacement happens only after that archive write succeeds. In-run status updates do not create history copies. Archive and latest files are separately atomic, not a distributed transaction.
  • Local deployment validation checks generated files only; it does not query live item, binding, run, or data readiness.

An overall DEGRADED result means the required workspace is usable, but one or more optional capabilities have failed or unknown evidence. Operators inspect the linked readiness report before presenting those optional capabilities. FAILED means a required capability is not ready.

Standard and full-demo run the profile-aware live verifier after their pipeline gates. Full-demo verification runs after automatic ontology, Data Agent, and exact task-flow completion. Verification is read-only: it does not trigger a second pipeline. Required failed/unknown evidence fails deployment; optional failed/unknown evidence marks the journal and linked readiness report DEGRADED. Operators may explicitly trigger the profile's post-publish pipeline only with retail-setup verify --env <env> --run-pipeline.

The verifier, report, and local contracts are implemented. Historical full-demo evidence predates these changes. Fresh readiness-consistency and remote smoke tests remain open, along with recent manual-stream evidence under IMP-013.

items.text:

  • Specifications: exact interfaces, schemas, workflows, states, errors.

  • Security: threats, controls, assumptions, and residual risks.
  • Guides: derived user procedures.

Module backlogs contain only Open and Settled — do not reopen.

items.title: Temporary artifacts
items.text:
Keep dated plans, raw findings, generated context, and migration audits out of the published source tree. Move their lasting requirements, decisions, and unresolved work into the relevant technical pages before deleting the temporary files or replacing them with pointers.

The prior docs/superpowers/ implementation plans were removed after durable content was promoted. Temporary planning material must remain outside the published source tree.

The pinned Zensical version does not support exclude_docs or draft_docs (upstream tracking). Omitting a page from nav does not prevent publication or indexing. Do not add an unsupported exclusion setting as a security control.

The decision experience, ML/AI backlog, and THREAT-009 / SEC-012 replace the former root-level action and customer experience drafts. Routing has a specification; evaluation questions and the CIO walkthrough have dedicated guides. Raw response logs and generated HTML/diagram exports were removed after preserving unresolved ontology, model-quality, action, and security concerns. The action-framework URL remains a pointer for existing component links. No old response count, latency, or deployment claim is current verification.

tests/docs/test_documentation_boundary.py checks source publication boundaries, navigation, links, and requirement/threat ownership. Review the built output as well. Immutable historical versions use their tag's source; changing current docs does not retroactively validate or sanitize those sites.

items.title: Operational output
items.text:
setup_run_log appends a unique setup-attempt record, table-level completion records, and a final completion or failure record. Reusing an existing run_id is rejected so retries cannot create ambiguous duplicate history.

Setup-02 generates and validates dimensions without publishing them. Setup-03 through setup-09 regenerate the same deterministic dimensions and generate the facts as handoff tables. Setup-10 (setup-10-publish-silver) is the single Silver publication boundary. write_all stages every candidate under a run-scoped <schema>_stage schema, validates schema and row counts, captures existing Delta versions, then promotes. An attempted promotion failure restores pre-existing targets and drops newly created targets in reverse order.

Terminal publication states distinguish data recovery from staging cleanup: COMPLETED, FAILED, ROLLED_BACK, ROLLBACK_FAILED, COMPLETED_CLEANUP_FAILED, and ROLLED_BACK_CLEANUP_FAILED.

COMPLETED_CLEANUP_FAILED means data promotion succeeded: the writer returns success with a warning and logs retained staging artifacts. Readiness reports cleanup as degradation, not failed historical data. Rollback states still represent failed publication attempts even when restoration succeeded.

Historical Silver replacement is blocked once the configured <lakehouse>.<silver_db>._watermarks table exists, even if it has no rows. Stop writers and use coordinated Silver/checkpoint recovery before rebuilding history; deleting watermarks alone would allow replay to corrupt rebuilt data. The writer guard is not a distributed lock, so operators must serialize historical and streaming writers.

The retained historical loader must materialize the exact ordered TABLES field names and types, not sampled/inferred Parquet schemas. Synthetic fixture data must not silently stand in for a missing or incompatible historical source.

items.title: Generation order
items.text: The engine creates dimensions and date context, then candidate store demand. It resolves inventory-constrained fulfillment before publishing sales, returns, payments, promotions, attribution, sensors, and stock ledgers. Online orders, marketing, store activity, and Gold output retain their related contracts. Reusable intermediate data is cached where repeated calculations would otherwise recompute it.

items.title: Execution performance
items.text:
Generation is a dependency graph of stages (STAGES in generation/engine.py). Each stage names its inputs, its outputs, and the setup notebook that runs it:

Notebook Stages Waits for setup-03-generate-sales candidate receipts, fulfillment plan setup-01 setup-04-generate-online-orders online orders setup-01 setup-05-generate-marketing background impressions setup-01 setup-06-generate-returns-and-promotions returns, promotions setup-03 setup-07-generate-store-activity store operations, foot traffic, BLE setup-03 setup-08-generate-inventory inventory, logistics, and stockout ledgers setup-03 setup-09-attribute-marketing last-touch attribution setup-03 to 06 setup-10-publish-silver invariants and atomic Silver publication setup-02 to 04, 06 to 09

setup-pipeline follows the same dependency graph at notebook level; a test checks that the two graphs agree. Independent notebooks run in separate Spark sessions. At most six run at once, within the session concurrency that capacity sizing reserves for required ML. Setup-10 runs its invariant checks and per-table staging, validation, and promotion concurrently; every phase still completes for all tables before the next starts, and any promotion failure rolls back every table.

Gold (setup-11-build-gold) runs in ml-required alongside model training. It shares a lane with customer segmentation, keeping that pipeline within six sessions. Inside a notebook, up to six ready stages run concurrently. A stage writes its own outputs one after another so related cached plans are never built concurrently. Completion order and the notebook split do not change the output; a test compares the notebook path with single-session generate_all row for row.

Stage outputs that a later notebook needs are written as gen__<stage>__<output> Delta tables in the Silver staging schema. Each records the generation fingerprint (a hash of the generation configuration) in its Delta commit, and loading a handoff produced for another configuration fails. Setup-10 promotes single-handoff facts directly from their handoffs and drops every handoff only after publication succeeds, so a failed publication can be retried without regenerating. Within a notebook, other stage frames are checkpointed under Files/setup/_checkpoints/<notebook> in the Lakehouse rather than on executors. Later steps therefore do not depend on an executor's local data surviving autoscaling or executor loss. generate_all (local tests) runs the whole graph in one session with the same checkpoints, which stay on the executors when no folder is given.

Generation output never depends on Spark partitioning, so each notebook sizes spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to the configured receipt-line volume (about one million lines per partition, between 200 and 8,192) and lets adaptive execution coalesce small shuffles. Materializing each stage before dependants consume it also means later plans start from small leaves instead of re-analyzing the full upstream lineage on the driver. The inventory policy runs in Python workers through mapInArrow, which moves demand and events in Arrow column batches rather than pickling each row. BLE zone selection, ping sequencing, and zone changes are per-visit array operations, so the ping stream is never shuffled.

items.title: Retail behavior and calibration
items.text:
Historical store demand starts with open-hour visitors. A seeded negative-binomial count controls arrival variability; each visitor has a purchase decision using store/hour conversion propensity. Footfall uses this same visitor grid, not receipts divided by a fixed conversion percentage. The existing five zone counts conserve hourly visitors exactly. These are allocated sensor counts, not a physical trajectory model.

Customer selection has persistent, long-tailed visit propensities and geography affinity. Continuous customer spending propensity and quick, regular, family, and bulk shopping missions shape basket sizes. Most lines share the trip's department preference; others permit cross-department shopping. Product popularity is persistent, price-sensitive, and uneven. Catalog selection excludes products not yet launched.

avg_ticket_target calibrates expected line counts against actual eligible catalog prices, category quantities, tax, and expected discounts. basket_lambda limits the nominal mean line count; neither setting changes catalog prices or forces every ticket to the target. One-line minimums and expensive catalogs can make a target unattainable. Report distributions and calibration error rather than truncating individual tickets. Consumables and durables use different geometric quantity distributions, with single units most common and no artificial four-unit maximum.

Promotion exposure precedes basket-size sampling and raises additional-item demand. Discounts still precede tax, and receipt/payment amounts reconcile in integer cents. This models coupon-driven basket expansion, not fitted causal price elasticity or a market-basket model learned from real transactions.

The shared draw implementation uses Box-Muller normal draws and an exact integer-shape negative-binomial distribution (sum of geometric draws). All decisions retain stable key/seed salts, independent of Spark partitioning. The changed simulation intentionally produces different data from older code with the same seed; reproducibility requires the same code, dictionaries, configuration, and date window.

items.title: Inventory feedback and unfulfilled demand
items.text:
The replenishment policy covers every selling store/SKU. It learns from past attempted demand, considers on-hand and pending deliveries/accepted restocks, and orders case-pack quantities against coverage and safety-stock targets. Opening stock is seeded independently of future transactions. Deterministic delivery delays allow depletion and recovery rather than permanent negative balances or a blanket zero floor.

A candidate line is fulfilled in full only when its stock is available. Rejected lines are omitted from realized receipts; empty receipts disappear. Receipt totals, discounts, tax, payments, and refunds are reconciled against fulfilled lines. The return plan preserves sampled dates and identities while only actual fulfilled/refunded units can be restocked. Dependent promotions and attribution consume realized sales, not attempted demand.

fact_store_inventory_txn appends two long audit columns after the existing schema: requested_quantity and unfulfilled_quantity. LOST_SALE rows record rejected demand with zero physical quantity; they must not decrement stock. Store/DC/truck transfers share the fulfillment plan, and inventory positions exclude deliveries outside the requested history. Physical-stock invariants verify nonnegative balances, running-sum conservation, opening stock, receipt/refund mirrors, demand accounting, and transfer conservation.

Streaming replay preserves historical demand-audit fields. Older ledgers without these columns derive fulfilled requested quantities from negative SALE movements and use zero unfulfilled demand, because the older producer did not record lost sales. This is read-side compatibility only: writes still require the declared target schema. Regenerate historical setup or explicitly migrate the target before resuming streaming against an older table. Live deltas have zero unfulfilled demand; this is not evidence of measured lost demand in the live scenario generator.

The current baseline assumes unlimited just-in-time supply at the DC and SKU-specific shipments. It does not optimize fleet routing or simulate supplier capacity constraints. Historical online orders retain their separate synthetic fulfillment model; do not interpret its statuses as reservations against the store policy.

items.title: Historical/live boundary
items.text:
The stream notebook embeds the shared basket/catalog/quantity code at build time. It emits a variable-length receipt-line array with matching item counts, promotion products, line discounts, tax, header totals, and payments. Online live headers retain their existing no-discount contract. Missing store tax or an empty/missing eligible catalog is an error, not a synthetic $9.99 price.

Live catalog launch eligibility is snapshotted when the stream starts; restart the stream to pick up newly launched products or changed catalog/profile data. The rate source remains an operator-controlled demonstration pace, not the historical visitor-arrival process. Live event scenarios and historical online fulfillment retain their explicitly synthetic scheduling assumptions; shared basket behavior does not imply a persistent live supply-chain simulator.

items.title: Statistical acceptance
items.text: Use multiple seeds and short and multi-year windows. Check ticket and basket percentiles, customer purchase-frequency dispersion, SKU concentration, conversion variability, stockout duration/recovery, inventory conservation, and historical/live basket distributions. Keep legitimate price points, integer quantities, business constraints, and calibrated model-score plateaus; do not add jitter to hide them. Local synthetic calibration targets are demo assumptions, not claims about measured industry distributions.

items.title: Invariants
items.text:
Current invariant checks include:

  • key uniqueness and required foreign keys;
  • non-null event dates;
  • online-order header/line integrity;
  • pricing, tax, and promotion consistency;
  • seven-day last-touch uniqueness and impression/purchase linkage;
  • attributed revenue, discount, tax, total, and payment reconciliation;
  • stockout location exclusivity;
  • physical stock, transfer conservation, and explicit unfulfilled-demand accounting;
  • truck timing and inventory relationships;
  • sales only within each store's operating hours;
  • no receipt line sold before its product's launch date;
  • returns posted strictly after the originating sale (never same-day);
  • product lifecycle dates present (no degenerate lifecycles).

utility/src/retail_setup/generation/invariants.py enforces the shared live/batch invariants: operating hours, product launch eligibility, return timing, lifecycle presence, and validated profile controls.

items.title: Naming compatibility
items.text: New columns use snake_case, but current TMDL compatibility requires explicit legacy exceptions such as ID, StoreNumber, CustomerId, StoreID, ReceiptId, Source, Subtotal, and __index_level_0__. These exceptions are documented in schemas.py and must not be silently normalized in a transform.

items.title: Store profiles and derived defaults
items.text:
Supported profiles are supercenter, grocery, hardware, and luxury. Current derived defaults include:

  • silver_db = ag
  • gold_db = au
  • dc_count = max(1, store_count // 10)
  • customer_count = max(store_count * 1000, 5000)
  • online_orders_per_day = store_count * 8
  • transactions_per_store_day = 400
  • return_rate = 0.01
  • brands_per_product = 3
  • truck_capacity = 15000

In-store customer assignment reserves a deterministic 10% cohort whose purchases stop at seeded, staggered dates inside the generation window. Post-cutoff receipts are reassigned to active customers. This preserves pre-churn behavior while guaranteeing forward-looking churn labels across chronological ML splits.

items.title: Removed active-path behavior
items.text: Local FastAPI control, DuckDB persistence, parquet export, Blob upload, Event Hubs, outbox, dead-letter queue (DLQ), and Prometheus services are not part of the supported Fabric-native contract.
