items.title: Decision experience and action boundaries
items.text: This specification defines the proposed action layer and Retail customer experience (CX). It replaces dated implementation plans; the Fabric profile manifest still defines deployment selections. REQ-MLAI-005 remains proposed: the presence of replay/app code does not prove the complete scenario, shared hosting, or production execution.

items.title: Current local application boundary
items.text:
app/backend/main.py routes questions to Fabric Data Agent and Ontology MCP services, and to inventory/retention tools in app/backend/agents.py. app/backend/replay.py supplies synthetic replay responses. Inspect the selected mode before presenting any answer as live.

Live proposals are local JSON records managed by app/backend/proposals.py. Approving a record changes its local status; it does not submit a purchase order, send a campaign, or call an ERP, CRM, pricing, or workforce system. app/backend/eventhouse.py sends telemetry on daemon threads and suppresses ingestion errors. It is best-effort telemetry, not a guaranteed audit trail. These limitations are tracked by THREAT-009 and SEC-012.

items.title: Native availability pack
items.text:
REQ-MLAI-006 covers a separate native experience, not a claim that the full proposed CX application is implemented. The deployment entry point is deploy/scripts/deploy_operations_planning.py; configuration and operator steps live in the deployment guide.

Configuration enables the pack by default whenever the profile provisions Eventhouse and a semantic model, with include_plan=false. Because Fabric can reject Operations Agent creation, an operations-only deployment step is non-required: its failure is journaled and the deployment continues. Readiness expects the Operations Agent as a non-required item, so its absence degrades rather than fails readiness. Explicitly including the Plan restores a required, fail-closed step.

operations_planning.include_plan=false selects Operations Agent and its draft notebook independently. It bypasses only unselected Planning prerequisites, not authentication or validation for a selected Plan. No model connection is changed and no fixed credentials are created. Agent instructions and notebook notes route human review to the Lakehouse draft table and existing SSO report instead of a nonexistent Plan. Readiness excludes the unselected Plan. Use this mode when organizational policy prohibits fixed credentials; native Planning is unsupported in that environment, not silently simulated.

The bounded Protect weekend availability scenario uses store IDs 1-5 and product IDs 1-20 in both the agent and Plan. It takes current au.stockout_risk, joins the next seven forecast days from au.demand_forecast, and resolves product names through ag.dim_products. Missing, non-finite, negative forecast, duplicate-grain, out-of-scope, stale, and future evidence fail closed. A known negative stock ledger is not inbound supply; the available-stock measure has a zero floor. Inventory's last movement time can precede the forecast's common source anchor. Both timestamps remain explicit; publication time does not replace either. Case identity includes store, product, and both source timestamps. Risk retains its own risk_horizon_days (default three); it is not relabeled as seven-day risk. The Plan's additive Next 7 Days measures slice forecast dates rather than filtering horizon metadata: the demand model defaults to fourteen days. Existing full-horizon measures remain unchanged.

fabric/operations/01-availability-tables.kql owns ops_availability_signals and ops_case_actions. These are selected-pack tables, not the optional retail event stream. Seeding them must not satisfy stream watermarks, ingestion, or checkpoint freshness. Consumers select the latest monitoring event per case. Historical reorder rows do not establish open commitments, confirmed inbound, reservations, or shared DC availability.

retail-availability-operations publishes stopped with its KQL database and instructions. The REST publisher omits the empty playbook object so the UI can generate it. The public definition API rejects FabricJobAction, so the publisher follows item creation with the UI-native OA workload call and binds prepare-replenishment-case using itemArtifactId, itemWorkspaceId, and RunNotebook. It requires exact workload-service readback of one KQL source and one action. The public service may normalize a KQL source ID to all zeroes in definition readback; the workload readback is authoritative for configured source/action details. Successful publication requires shouldRun=false. Teams destination setup, playbook generation/review, and deliberate activation remain operator steps. Deployment does not silently enable autonomous purchasing.

The prepare-replenishment-case action validates a selected case against live signals, freezes the inspected snapshot, and merges a DRAFT into <lakehouse>.ops.replenishment_cases. It never overwrites an existing case. Existing APPROVED or RESOLVED cases are not relabeled or audited as DRAFT. An idempotently tagged Kusto audit follows the durable Delta write. The two services are not an atomic transaction: failures propagate and a retry can finish the missing audit without duplicating the draft. Historical ag/au tables and external purchasing systems remain unchanged.

retail-replenishment is a native Plan, not another autonomous agent. Its supported PlanV1 definition binds the deployed semantic model through an explicitly supplied shared Power BI Semantic Model connection (PowerBIDatasets, OAuth2 or ServicePrincipal). Separately, the underlying Direct Lake-to-data connection must use fixed credentials, not Automatic/SSO. WorkspaceIdentity can be valid for that underlying hop but is not a supported substitute for the Plan-to-model connection. The deploy inspects both without automatically rebinding the existing model. The deploy must reject missing connection or unacknowledged billing before creating either component of a combined request. --operations-only is an explicit partial operation when configuration still includes the Plan. A persistent include_plan=false selection requires only the Operations components.

Native planning what-if inputs are assumptions until confirmed. There is no public run-Optimize API in this implementation and no automatic bridge from Plan writeback to an ERP, or from a case row into a new semantic-model table. The planner uses the case's store/product identifiers for the human handoff. Native application-database bootstrap, interactive model access, approval workflows, and SQL writeback need separate in-product acceptance. Plan creation/opening can start a non-cancellable 30-day billable session.

The source definitions are not added to unsupported fabric-cicd item types. Native item APIs perform idempotent name resolution, bounded long-running-operation polling, and definition readback. Duplicate names, untrusted polling hosts, denied requests, and mismatches fail explicitly. Supported existing task-flow bindings remain unchanged until native artifact-type support is established.

items.title: Responsibility split
items.text:
flowchart LR
    User[Question or decision] --> Router[Application orchestrator]
    Router --> Metrics[Semantic model: measures and broad aggregates]
    Router --> Graph[Ontology: named entities and relationships]
    Router --> Actions[Domain action tools]
    Metrics --> Evidence[Source, grain, time window, limitations]
    Graph --> Evidence
    Evidence --> Actions
    Actions --> Draft[Local proposal]
    Draft --> Human[Approve, dismiss, or scenario override]
    Human --> Package[Draft action package]
    Human -. best-effort telemetry .-> Eventhouse[Eventhouse]

Use semantic-model measures for rankings, period comparisons, conversion, velocity, margin, and prediction rollups. Use the ontology for named-entity context, serving-node/compatible-SKU paths, and evidence relationships. Do not substitute an unbounded graph scan for broad analytical queries. The active live generator writes directly to Eventhouse through Spark Kusto, not through Eventstream.

items.title: Proposed action roster
items.text:
Only inventory and retention have local action-tool implementations. The remaining domain tools and multi-agent composition require acceptance and verification under the ML/AI backlog.

Domain Evidence and decision Proposed draft Inventory Stockout risk, forecast, balances, and covering reorders; serving DC/truck path Reorder, expedite, rebalance, or safety-stock review Retention Churn, segment/LTV, purchase context, and market-basket cross-sell Cohort win-back brief and offer suggestions Pricing Elasticity, promotion discount, margin, and price recommendation Price/promotion review with quantified assumptions Store operations Velocity, conversion, checkout dwell, and anomalies Staffing, lane, investigation, or store task Fulfillment Predicted truck dwell, lane delays, fulfillment mix, and uncovered demand Dispatch/route/fulfillment review Merchandising Association lift/confidence, sell-through, spread, and returns Bundle, placement, assortment, or quality review

An actionable recommendation requires a quantified gap, a decision owner, and a reversible first step. Informational executive, channel, segment, forecast, journey, or association questions must not silently create actions. Composite opportunities include revenue-at-risk retention, stockout/sales protection, margin recovery, and a prioritized per-store action list. Illustrative financial impacts are assumptions, not realized savings.

items.title: Proposed guardrails
items.text:
Tier Meaning Required boundary before enabling execution T0 Inform without a write Identify source and uncertainty T1 Draft a local proposal Display evidence; human review before promotion T2 Reversible external execution Explicit authenticated approval and durable outcome record T3 High-impact price, offer, or large reorder Approval plus reason, limits, and audit evidence

Only the local draft/review boundary is in scope today. Future tools must validate IDs against source rows, use configurable numeric thresholds, check covering/repeated actions for idempotency, cap fan-out, and retain the asker, evidence, tier, approver, outcome, and decision time. These are proposed controls, not guarantees of the existing prototype.

items.title: Proposed Retail CX scenario
items.text:
The fictional Aster & Pine Outfitters scenario, Protect the Winner, follows Dana Reyes, a regional merchandising lead:

  1. A declining Performance Footwear category contains a growing Momentum Runner product family. Compare periods and store/channel contribution.
  2. Find named products/SKUs, stock snapshots, stores, regions, channels, and fulfillment nodes through explicit relationships.
  3. Activate sufficiently covered stores, replenish high-velocity constrained stores, and propose compatible transfers from slower excess-stock stores.
  4. Remove one source store with a required human reason; retain the original recommendation and recalculate candidates.
  5. Produce a draft transfer/replenishment list, activation brief, execution checklist, evidence bundle, owner, review date, and decision/override log.

Reserved inventory remains at its certified fulfillment-node/product grain. Never infer store allocation, SKU compatibility, or a relationship absent from source data. Separate selling, fulfilling, and source stores; use one inventory snapshot/as-of time, aggregate numerators and denominators before ratios, and align periods with the scenario's fiscal calendar. Distinguish observed facts, derived values, and recommendations; return unsupported when required evidence is missing.

items.title: Proposed experience and replay contract
items.text:
• Decision Cockpit: synthetic label, report or replay, morning brief, guided prompts, route badge, and evidence/query trace.
  • Story Studio: chapter navigation, Work/Fabric/Foundry/Web IQ cards, signal state, independent Question Lab, explicit action trigger, decisions, and links to the canvas and operations.
  • Decision Canvas: signal, diagnosis, certified-grain constraint, recommendation, override, draft package, owner, and review state.
  • Ontology Explorer: entities, properties, relationships, and highlighted paths used by the selected answer.
  • Agent Operations: proposal states, approvals/dismissals/overrides, modeled impact assumptions, evidence ownership, and live/replay provenance.
  • Walkthrough: capability explanation, validated click path, and fallback.

Replay and live modes must use the same response contracts and components. Replay must visibly say REPLAY — SYNTHETIC DATA and work without Fabric credentials. A versioned fixture must include KPIs, prompts, metric/graph answers, graph paths, cards, override response, action package, and telemetry. Do not silently present fixture data as a successful live query.

items.title: Proposed data and packaging
items.text:
Generate all records independently, never by copying, sampling, perturbing, or hashing customer records. Use fictional vocabulary and opaque keys; keep real contact details, credentials, environment identifiers, and customer response logs out of source, fixtures, and screenshots. Review generated content before publication (SEC-003, SEC-010, SEC-012).

The scenario package needs a fixed seed/date/scale run ID, source-separated JSONL or Parquet, file checksums, row counts, reconciliation results, and golden answers. It should intentionally exercise category decline/product growth, three high-velocity low-cover stores, four activation-ready stores, two excess-stock stores, an override, and an aggregate-grain DC constraint. These are scenario requirements, not changes to historical TABLES.

Potential future entities include ProductFamily, SKU, InventorySnapshot, FulfillmentNode, TradingSignal, DecisionScenario, Recommendation, Evidence, Decision, Override, and ActionPackage. Extend the authoritative model and ontology contracts before claiming these relationships exist.

Reuse the standalone app before considering hosted delegated-identity or Fabric Workload packaging. Keep backend/UI contracts portable; a new agent framework is optional, not a prerequisite. Shared hosting, service identity, secret management, durable approvals/audit, external adapters, and a native Fabric shell require separate design and tests.

items.title: Verification still required
items.text: Run the complete five-act story in replay without credentials, assert answers and override transitions, verify synthetic labels and no production writes, and exercise degraded live-service behavior. Separately validate live Fabric/model/ontology bindings and telemetry delivery with retained run evidence. Golden replay answers are not live readiness proof.

items.title: Pipeline sequence
items.text:
The deployment separates data setup, required Reporting dependencies, and extended ML:

  1. setup-pipeline runs setup notebooks 01 through 11.
  2. ml-required runs demand forecast (06), customer segmentation (08), churn (09), stockout (12), market-basket mining (07), and promotion/elasticity analysis (10) producers serially, in that order, to avoid oversubscribing the shared Spark pool.
  3. 15-validate-required-ml-contract runs only after all six producers succeed, and validates all six required output tables.
  4. Reporting can publish only after that exact pipeline run reaches terminal Completed.
  5. full-demo runs ml-optional (notebooks 11 and 13) and ml-experimental (notebook 14, which consumes price_elasticity produced by the required run) after Reporting.

Optional or experimental failure cannot block required Reporting. Ontology creation is a separate preview phase after Reporting and extended ML, but full-demo executes it automatically. The task-flow metadata mirrors the runtime order as Required ML Reporting Gate -> Reporting -> Post-Reporting Extended ML.

items.title: ML contracts
items.text:
The repository includes demand forecast, market-basket, customer segmentation, churn, promotion effectiveness, journey, stockout, delivery, and dynamic pricing notebooks.

contracts/retail-demo.json records typed support tiers and one contract for each of their 14 outputs:

Tier Outputs Required demand_forecast, customer_segments, churn_predictions, stockout_risk, product_recommendations, price_elasticity Optional promoted product_associations, journey_patterns, zone_transitions, zone_dwell_stats, dwell_predictions Experimental promotion_lift, pricing_constraints, pricing_recommendations

Every contract identifies its producer and source tables, exact output schema and grain, as-of and lineage fields, intended use, and limitations. Producer notebooks declare the same schema and validate types and non-null constraints immediately before writing that exact physical target. Required contracts additionally reference the active Tabular Model Definition Language (TMDL) projection and the runtime validator. These checks keep the manifest aligned with the physical schema.

For all six required outputs, generated_at is the true Gold publication timestamp and model_run_id identifies that generation. Source/business cutoffs remain separate lineage: source_as_of for demand, segmented_at for segments, prediction_date for churn, and predicted_at plus inventory_as_of for stockout. product_recommendations and price_elasticity carry the same generated_at, model_run_id, and schema_version lineage columns as the original four; their business as-of remains computed_at. Readiness orders and ages generated_at from the same row as a nonblank run ID; it never treats a business as-of date as a generation timestamp.

The Reporting gate requires nonempty results from market-basket mining and promotion/elasticity analysis, alongside demand, segmentation, churn, and stockout outputs. This includes product_recommendations and price_elasticity in the required tier.

The runtime validator creates no tables. It rejects missing/empty required outputs, incompatible columns or types, null/duplicate grain keys, invalid probabilities or bounds, NaN or infinity in any floating output, missing as-of/lineage, and incomplete forecast horizons. Repository validation parses the validator's required grain, as-of, lineage, probability, and horizon rules and compares them exactly with the manifest.

Optional outputs may be empty when the business preconditions for a result do not exist. For example, sparse baskets can produce no association rules, and a delivery run can have no currently open arrivals to score. In those cases the producer overwrites the target with an empty table that still has the exact contract schema. Readiness accepts that empty snapshot only when the owning optional pipeline has exact, recent terminal-success evidence.

Demand evaluation freezes store/product eligibility at the training cutoff; current production inference selects its cohort independently. Churn and stockout partition on label-availability dates and purge 90-day and three-day forward-label horizons, respectively.

items.title: Stockout inventory semantics
items.text:
The inventory ledger retains signed balances; a deficit is not a negative number of available units. Notebook 12 selects the latest inventory event per store/product/day, then derives model current_inventory as max(balance, 0) for known balances. Both training and current inference use that same snapshot function, so derived days_of_inventory and inventory ratios remain nonnegative. This does not rewrite the underlying ledger.

Unknown balances remain null, and the producer rejects any null inventory balance before training. A null must never be converted to zero by Spark's greatest null-skipping behavior. Notebook 15 continues to reject negative inventory/demand/coverage, invalid classes/horizons/ranks, and inconsistent as-of timestamps. Its stockout error reports per-rule violation counts. utility/tests/generation/test_stockout_contract_runtime.py executes the producer feature functions and the downstream domain validator together.

Churn retains hidden nullable is_churned_actual solely as a deprecated compatibility projection and always writes it as null. All formerly exposed required columns remain present, so a failed required-ML gate can leave the previous Reporting artifact query-compatible while Reporting publication stays blocked.

Optional and experimental corrections are also contract-bound:

  • recommendation support, confidence, and lift come from one singleton-pair market-basket rule;
  • promotion prices use net extended cents per unit and comparisons include only episodes with complete baseline and post windows inside each store's observed receipt range;
  • delivery training uses matched cusn Bronze lifecycle events (cusn is the Lakehouse schema that exposes Eventhouse tables as read-only shortcuts), partitions on departure-time label availability with a purge, and scores only unmatched arrivals with arrival-known features; missing training sources fail, while no inference-ready arrivals publish an empty contract-valid snapshot;
  • pricing uses a non-null no-estimate evidence sentinel, advances cooldown state only for accepted price changes, and applies the log-log quantity response (new_price / old_price) ** elasticity - 1.

items.title: Semantic-model dependency
items.text:
The active semantic model currently references six ML output tables:

  • churn_predictions
  • customer_segments
  • demand_forecast
  • stockout_risk
  • product_recommendations
  • price_elasticity

core does not publish ML or Reporting. standard and full-demo use the required runtime gate; a skipped, failed, cancelled, deduplicated, or unknown run status performs no Reporting publication and records a journal failure. On an upgrade, an already deployed report is left in place rather than replaced with an artifact built against an unvalidated schema.

items.title: Ontology
items.text:
30-create-ontology.ipynb:

  • discovers the current workspace and source items;
  • represents business entities and relationships;
  • binds Lakehouse tables and Eventhouse time-series context;
  • prefers update-in-place for an existing ontology;
  • falls back to delete/recreate with polling and retry behavior when needed.

Ontology creation is not part of the required ML pipeline. Full-demo runs it automatically after Reporting and extended ML, but only after live tenant/capacity preflight passes. post-ontology reruns this phase for recovery.

The Fabric ontology public definition EntityTypeProperty schema doesn't currently expose field descriptions. After creating or updating the public definition, the deployment notebook uses the same Digital Operations authoring API as the Fabric UI to apply descriptions to every regular and time-series property, then reads the entity types back and fails if any description wasn't persisted.

Descriptions come from source metadata when available, otherwise from deterministic field context. The notebook identity obtains a Power BI token, exchanges it for a Digital Operations workload token, and sends credentials only to HTTPS service URLs whose hosts end in .analysis.windows.net or .pbidedicated.windows.net; any other Fabric-returned URL fails the run. The apply-and-verify sequence retries up to five times only for HTTP 404, 409, 429, 500, 502, 503, or 504; other failures fail immediately.

items.title: New-experience (TMDL) publisher
items.text:
The notebook above publishes the old entity-type JSON format, which Fabric retires on Jan 31, 2027 (ENH-010). deploy/scripts/deploy_ontology.py publishes the replacement definition. Full-demo deployment runs it as the non-required publish-ontology-tmdl step, after ensure-ontology and before the Data Agents are published. A failure keeps the existing ontology and degrades the run instead of failing it. Once the ontology is in TMDL format, ensure_ontology no longer runs the legacy notebook, so the migration is not reverted. Live acceptance is still pending.

deploy/scripts/_ontology_model.py renders the definition deterministically from the physical contracts, not from runtime inspection:

  • Silver tables come from utility/src/retail_setup/generation/schemas.py, Gold ML outputs from ml_contracts in contracts/retail-demo.json, and Bronze event tables from fabric/kql_database/01-create-tables.kql.
  • All tables are DirectLake partitions behind one Sql.Database expression for the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint, in schemas ag, au, and cusn. Each partition also carries the ONT_* annotations (workspace, Lakehouse item ID/name/kind, SQL endpoint, pin time) that Fabric uses to identify the backing item. Without them Data Agents can't resolve the ontology's underlying source. The publisher fails if readback drops them. Eventhouse time series bind through the Bronze cusn shortcuts. The publisher lists Tables/cusn in OneLake, and missing shortcuts drop only their bindings.
  • The model has the same 12 entities and 17 relationship names as the notebook; three of the relationships use junction tables. Keys and properties use snake_case column names, and time-series properties are named <event_table>_<column> and ordered by ingest_timestamp.
  • TOM relationships that retail_model marks inactive are also inactive here. Each event table has exactly one active outgoing relationship, so the TOM graph has no ambiguous active paths.
  • Descriptions are native /// comments, so the authoring-API workaround and its token exchange are unnecessary in this path.
  • Lineage tags are UUIDv5 values of stable element names, so updates replace elements in place.
  • Semantic-model DAX measures are not published as metrics. TMDL cannot express projected metrics, and the definition does not duplicate DAX as explicit metrics.

Publication behavior:

Existing item Action None Create RetailOntology_AutoGen TMDL format (.platform config.version 2.0) updateDefinition in place Old format (definition.json or EntityTypes/ parts) Create and verify RetailOntology_AutoGen_tmdl, then delete the old item and rename the staged item; a failed staging readback leaves the old item intact

Readback must be in TMDL format and contain every generated table, entity, and rule part. The service elides defaults, so readback compares element sets rather than text. Evidence is written to deploy/.generated/<env>/ontology-report.json. Run python -m deploy.scripts.deploy_ontology --render <dir> to inspect the definition without service calls.

items.title: Business rules
items.text: deploy/scripts/_ontology_rules.py publishes nine natural-language rules (ENH-011): minimum margin, MSRP ceiling, price-change cadence, aged-inventory markdown, pricing approval, return window, stockout definition and risk bands, replenishment policy, and churn definition. Each numeric value is checked against the code that enforces it by tests/deploy/test_ontology_rules.py. Rules are guidance only; ontology does not execute them. Agents read them with the ontology MCP list_ontology_rules tool.

items.title: Data Agents
items.text:
Source-controlled Data Agent definitions require target-specific rebinding. They are staged after ontology creation in the same full-demo deployment. That completion phase rewrites:

  • workspaceId
  • semantic-model artifactId
  • ontology artifactId

Current semantic-model draft and published datasource snapshots select every retail_model table, column, and measure (the data is synthetic) and include dataSourceInstructions and userDescription; .platform descriptions distinguish semantic-model and ontology scope. The ontology agent binds the TMDL ontology as an ontology-as-context source (ontologies/RetailOntology_AutoGen/ontology.json, schema dataAgent/definition/ontology/1.0.0). That schema has no datasource instructions, so every ontology entity type is selected and the stage aiInstructions carry the answer rules. Both agents' instructions keep individual customers' names, addresses, phone numbers, and loyalty-card values out of answers. The legacy ontology-<name>/datasource.json binding fails against TMDL ontologies. Source schema validation and matching local draft/published snapshots do not prove remote publication, permissions, or behavior. Rebind and verify the deployed agents in Fabric. Mandatory per-agent governance metadata remains outside the default release; richer persona-specific instructions and approved-question packs remain optional under ENH-003.

items.title: Preview and support boundary
items.text: Ontology and related capabilities require explicit tenant capability checks. Semantic-model agents and ontology agents are separate features; failure or unavailability of one must not be presented as failure of the other.

items.title: Chat orchestrator: how questions are routed
items.text:
Retail Intelligence chat (app/) routes questions to the Fabric Data Agent, Ontology MCP, or an Inventory or Retention action agent. This page describes route selection and what happens when a data service cannot answer.

The orchestrator lives in app/backend/main.py (the /api/chat handler, _orchestrate, _route_with_reason, _action_route) plus the LLM classifier in app/backend/llm_router.py.

This describes local source behavior, not guaranteed live service responses. Replay bypasses live routing. Inspect the actual response trace and mode; fallback cannot make unavailable Fabric services or missing data ready. See decision and security boundaries.

items.title: 1. Destinations
items.text:
Route Backend Best for data-agent Fabric Data Agent over the retail_model semantic model (Direct Lake) Aggregates, KPIs, rankings, trends, time windows, ML rollups, and broad scans ontology Ontology MCP (entity relationships, including Eventhouse telemetry) A named customer's, product's, or store's related data; one-hop lookups inventory Inventory & Replenishment action agent Requests to act on stock or replenishment; returns a recommendation card and draft reorders retention Customer Retention action agent Requests to act on churn or retention; returns a recommendation card and draft campaign

The action agents (inventory, retention) return their own answers without fallback. For data-agent and ontology, the router ranks the two services: it tries one first and uses the other as a fallback.

items.title: 2. The decision flow
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A[POST /api/chat] --> B{surface override?<br/>data-agent / ontology}
    B -- yes --> Z[Use that backend only<br/>router = manual override]
    B -- no --> C{Real-time sales velocity?<br/>'last N minutes' + sold/sales}
    C -- yes --> D[Lite Ontology MCP<br/>bounded live event stream<br/>routedTo = ontology-lite]
    C -- no --> E{LLM intent router<br/>gpt-4o-mini, keyless AAD}

    E -- "route = inventory/retention" --> F[Action agent<br/>recommendation card + drafts]
    E -- "route = data-agent" --> G[order = data-agent → ontology]
    E -- "route = ontology" --> H[order = ontology → data-agent]
    E -- "LLM failed / disabled" --> K[Keyword fallback router]

    K --> K1{Action cue?<br/>'what should we do' + domain<br/>or direct verb reorder/win-back}
    K1 -- yes --> F
    K1 -- no --> K2{Data-Agent cue?<br/>total/sum/count/top/trend/churn…}
    K2 -- yes --> G
    K2 -- no --> K3{Ontology cue?<br/>deliver/supplies/linked/route…}
    K3 -- yes --> H
    K3 -- no --> G

    G --> P[Try first backend]
    H --> P
    P --> Q{Answered with rows?}
    Q -- yes --> R[Synthesize answer<br/>resolve ids → names/locations<br/>+ trace, routedTo]
    Q -- "no / error / empty / translator fail" --> S[Fall back to the other backend<br/>trace.fellBack = true]
    S --> T{Answered?}
    T -- yes --> R
    T -- no --> U[Graceful 'couldn't answer<br/>from either' message]

    F --> R
    D --> R
    Z --> P

items.title: 3. Step-by-step
items.text:
The handler evaluates these gates in order; the first match wins.

  1. Manual override (surface): if the request sets "surface": "data-agent" or "ontology", the handler uses only that backend, with no fallback. Debugging and the UI's force-a-source control use this override. The router label is manual override.

  2. Real-time sales-velocity shortcut: a regex matches questions such as "which sold the most in the last 15 minutes" using a last/past time window and a sales verb. The shortcut sends a fixed 15-minute store-sales query to the lite ontology over Store and receipt_created, returning routedTo = ontology-lite. It does not guarantee that arbitrary requested windows or product grain are honored. Historical Gold also has a latest-window snapshot, but that is not evidence of a current live window. Shortcut failure falls through to normal routing.

  3. LLM intent router (llm_router.classify): a temperature=0 JSON classification call uses Azure OpenAI gpt-4o-mini by default, authenticated through az login. Set RETAIL_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic to use Claude. It returns {"route", "reason"} using a system prompt and about 14 examples that encode this policy:

  4. A named entity and its related business, ML, or telemetry data go to ontology (Customer-360, "which stores are at risk of selling out White Truffle Powder", "for store S000028, how many stockout_detected events and which products").
  5. Aggregates, rankings, trends, ML rollups, and broad scans go to data-agent.
  6. An action verb (should, do, prevent, draft, create, reorder, replenish, launch, recommend) with a domain selects inventory or retention. "Which customers are at risk" is a lookup, not an action request.

The chosen route also sets the fallback order: data-agent → [data-agent, ontology]; ontology → [ontology, data-agent].

  1. Keyword fallback router: if the LLM call fails, times out, returns bad JSON, or is disabled (RETAIL_LLM_ROUTER=0), a deterministic keyword router provides a local fallback:
  2. _action_route selects the matching agent for an action cue (what should we do, recommend, how do we) plus an inventory or retention domain word, or a direct verb such as reorder, replenish, win-back, or retain.

  3. Otherwise, _route_with_reason tries data-agent first for cues such as total, sum, count, top, trend, churn, revenue, and %. It tries ontology first for cues such as deliver, supplies, linked, route, which stores, and connected to. With no cue, it defaults to data-agent first.

  4. Execution and fallback: the handler tries the chosen order in sequence. A backend fails (and falls through to the next) when it raises an HTTP/timeout error, returns empty / "no results", or the ontology translator emits a transient bad-query error after its retries. If the first succeeds, the second is never called. If both fail, the response says neither service could answer, rather than returning a 500.

  5. Answer synthesis and trace: the synthesis step resolves bare ontology store_id and product_id integers to store numbers, locations, and product names. Every response carries routedTo and a trace (router model, decision reason, steps, the exact MCP call, the reconstructed graph path, a raw-row preview, and whether it fellBack).

The store/product lookup helpers use the explicitly imported dax client to query semantic-model rows. tests/app/test_lookup_indexes.py covers the import and row-to-name mapping regression. This is local lookup coverage, not proof of a successful remote semantic-model query.

items.title: 4. Why two routers?
items.text: The LLM router distinguishes a lookup such as "which customers are at risk" from an action request such as "churn is rising, what do we do." The keyword router provides a deterministic route choice without a network call when the LLM is unavailable. Downstream Fabric calls can still fail; choosing a route does not guarantee an answer.

items.title: 5. Worked examples
items.text: Question Route Why "What were total net sales and gross margin company-wide?" data-agent Aggregate financial metric. "Give me the 360 view of the customer with loyalty card LC012783099." ontology Single named customer enriched with segment + churn + profile. "Which stores are at risk of selling out White Truffle Powder?" ontology 1‑hop lookup: a named product's stockout-risk prediction → linked stores (no action verb). "For store S000028, how many stockout_detected events and which products?" ontology One named store's own live event telemetry, walked to its affected products. "Which products sold the most in the last 15 minutes?" ontology-lite shortcut Currently uses a fixed store-sales query; inspect grain rather than treating this as a verified product answer. "How many customers are predicted to churn and their total LTV?" data-agent Aggregate count/value over the ML churn table. "Stock is running low. What should we do about it?" inventory Action cue and inventory domain select draft reorders. "Churn is rising. How do we retain customers?" retention Action cue and retention domain select a draft win-back campaign.

items.title: 6. Knobs
items.text:
Env var Effect RETAIL_LLM_ROUTER=0 Force the deterministic keyword router (skip the LLM). RETAIL_LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic (+ RETAIL_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) Route with Claude instead of gpt-4o-mini. RETAIL_ONTOLOGY_TIMEOUT Seconds the ontology MCP gets before the orchestrator falls back. Request body "surface": "data-agent"\|"ontology" Force one backend (no routing, no fallback). Request body "router": "keyword" Skip the LLM for that single request.

Only the routing model is configurable by this application. Fabric controls the models that translate natural language into DAX and ontology queries. The trace names the router model that selected the route.

items.title: Connected retail operational twins
items.text: This specification defines REQ-OPS-005: read-only views of stores, a warehouse/distribution center, and trucks, using single sign-on (SSO). The implementation is a native Power BI report on the existing Fabric semantic model. It does not deploy Digital Twin Builder, Planning, or Operations Agent products.

items.title: Components and scope
items.text:
retail-twins provides network overview, Store Twin, Warehouse Twin, and Truck Twin pages. Native Power BI visuals query the signed-in user's existing Direct Lake model. The optional local app's shared operator-token cache is not involved.

flowchart LR
    DC[Warehouse / DC] --> Shipment[Recorded shipment]
    Shipment --> Truck[Truck]
    Shipment --> Store[Store]
    Shipment --> SKU[Cargo SKU]
    Store --> Inventory[Inventory and risk]
    DC --> Stock[Warehouse inventory ledger]

The pilot includes one recorded DC, two trucks, up to five connected stores, and up to twenty products found in their cargo records. If fewer products are observed, the report shows that smaller set without inventing SKUs or route links. The model has no new physical geometry, GPS, temperature, driver assignments, reservations, or warehouse-bin data.

items.title: Source and cohort contract
items.text:
deploy/scripts/_twin_cohort.py selects from ag.fact_truck_moves, anchored to the newest event no later than the observation time, with a fourteen-day lookback. Discovery reads at most 10,000 route rows, and the selected network keeps at most 1,000 shipments. When a bound is exceeded, the cohort keeps the newest rows. It drops every row at the boundary timestamp and moves window_start just past it, so cargo and report queries cover a complete window. Missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent shipment identity still fails. Both trucks must belong to the same recorded DC network. Each truck's latest recorded destination is included before filling the store set.

ag.fact_truck_inventory supplies observed cargo product IDs, joined using both truck and shipment identity. All SQL parameters are bound values, not interpolated shipment strings. The saved cohort retains the actual route and shipment evidence. Shipment IDs document the selected network; they must not become a permanent filter that hides every future shipment.

The displayed state is the latest recorded state in the selected scope, with explicit source timestamps. Cohort selection time is not a replacement for inventory, operations, or movement timestamps. Historical/synthetic observations must not be labeled live telemetry.

items.title: Entity semantics
items.text:
Store state combines recorded operating events, signed and available stock, observed stockout probabilities, and zone activity. Zone activity is not exact occupancy or a count of unique shoppers. Risk retains the model's actual forecast horizon; it is not automatically seven-day risk.

Warehouse state shows signed inventory and a nonnegative available-stock view at DC/SKU grain. Neither is available-to-promise: reservations and confirmed commitments are not known. Recorded shipment counts retain their defined source-relative time window.

Truck state uses recorded shipment/status events, planned ETA/ETD, loading and unloading evidence, and the current selected shipment's cargo ledger. Unknown or ambiguous state stays unknown. A departed truck is not assigned an invented GPS location or next destination.

The delay comparison adds sixty minutes to a recorded ETA as a clearly labeled what-if. It does not change an actual timestamp, predict an observed delay, recompute stockout probabilities, or place an order.

items.title: Deployment and authorization
items.text:
twins.enabled is independent and defaults to true whenever the profile selects the semantic model and Report (standard or full-demo); core cannot select twins. Selected twins publish after Reporting through the non-required deploy-twins step: a failure degrades the run, and later steps still run. The targeted deploy.scripts.deploy_twins command can update an existing workspace without rerunning historical generation.

The publisher requires the existing Automatic/SSO semantic-model binding. It never creates a fixed-credential connection or changes model permissions. Normal Fabric report/model/OneLake authorization remains the access-control boundary; cohort filters and navigation are not row-level security. Deployment uses the operator's login only to author and inspect artifacts. Viewers use their own identity in Fabric/Power BI, not that operator token.

deploy/scripts/_twin_model.py merges only catalogued twin measures and missing physical columns required by their expressions into the live model. Partitions, expressions, roles, and unrelated measures remain intact; conflicting existing column mappings fail rather than being overwritten. Changed live definitions are backed up under the environment's generated directory. The publisher reads back the additions, tolerates only equivalent TMDL serialization, and checks SSO again. It refreshes Direct Lake framing before data queries, including on retries with unchanged metadata, so new physical columns and current source files are queryable. Refresh polling tracks the exact accepted request and never changes credentials on failure.

Publication uses the supported Report REST definition API and a runtime semantic-model GUID. It checks representative DAX queries for all three entity sets before publishing the report. Native item readback verifies the requested report definition. Disabled twins do not delete an existing report.

items.title: Evidence and acceptance
items.text:
deploy/.generated/<env>/twins-report.json records the cohort, source window, model changes and backup, DAX evidence, report identity/link, and outcome. The complete bounded cohort is preserved, not truncated into unusable placeholder entries.

Source tests cover deterministic selection, actual route joins, invalid and future evidence, model-merge isolation, template/model references, native bindings, and opt-in orchestration. These are separate from service checks. Native report acceptance additionally requires page rendering, selector/ navigation behavior, and appropriately scoped viewer access. A model query or a report item ID alone does not prove those interactive properties. The recorded deployment's native Report and DAX checks succeeded; automatic image export is disabled by tenant policy. Do not enable export or relax identity policy solely to bypass an acceptance-tool limitation.

items.title: Deployment readiness
items.text:
Record the environment, tenant, workspace, operator identity, commit, generated output path, and deployment run before changing resources.

After publication, verify:

  • required Fabric items and workspace folders;
  • KQL tables, functions, and materialized views;
  • notebook default-Lakehouse bindings;
  • pipeline notebook references;
  • semantic-model binding and required tables;
  • task-flow references;
  • optional ontology and agent rebinding;
  • Lakehouse SQL endpoint metadata visibility;
  • a minimal historical and live data query.

Local validate_deployment.py checks are required, but they do not establish live readiness.

The supported live command is:

retail-setup verify --env <env>

It is read-only by default and writes the redacted, atomic deploy/.generated/<env>/readiness-report.json. The 26-row taxonomy covers target identity (1), item inventory (2), live definitions and bindings (6), task flow (1), KQL objects (4), schedules (1), pipeline results (3), and freshness (8). Only unselected capabilities may be SKIPPED.

Required FAIL or UNKNOWN produces FAILED and exit 1. Optional FAIL or UNKNOWN produces DEGRADED and exit 3; full success exits 0, and command usage errors exit 2. The report stores bounded operational evidence, hashes, target IDs/names, and lineage only. It excludes tokens, definition payloads, business rows, and raw tenant-sensitive diagnostics.

DEGRADED means required capabilities are usable but one or more optional capabilities need attention. It is not equivalent to FAILED.

retail-setup verify --env <env> --run-pipeline is an explicit mutation. It starts only the profile-required post-publish pipeline and polls the exact job instance to terminal success. Missing, unknown, timed-out, stale, or mismatched evidence fails closed. The option is invalid when the profile has no such pipeline.

Standard and full-demo deployment run the read-only verification after their existing setup and required-ML gates. Deployment never adds --run-pipeline. A failed required check fails the deployment; optional readiness gaps mark the deploy journal DEGRADED. Core remains operator-executed: run setup notebooks 01-11, then invoke verification. Full-demo verification runs only after the ontology, both Data Agents, and the complete task flow have been created or validated in the same deploy.

The deploy plan also runs optional SQL endpoint metadata synchronization after post-Reporting ML. This tells Fabric's SQL endpoint about newly created Lakehouse tables. A synchronization failure degrades the journal; readiness still fails the deployment when a required table is not queryable.

items.title: Pipeline state
items.text:
Pipeline Current scope Current schedule state setup-pipeline Setup 01-10 (02-05 and 06-08 in parallel) On demand; mandatory for Reporting profiles historical-data-load Retained historical-load notebook On demand streaming-data-load Streaming Silver then Gold Schedule file present, disabled daily-maintenance Delta maintenance Schedule file present, disabled ml-required Demand, segmentation, churn, stockout, market-basket, and promotion/elasticity producers, then runtime contract validation Terminal Reporting gate ml-optional Promoted optional outputs Full-demo post-Reporting ml-experimental Experimental outputs (consumes price_elasticity from ml-required) Full-demo post-Reporting

Do not describe the disabled streaming schedule as an active five-minute or fifteen-minute service.

The streaming pipeline passes configured Lakehouse/schema parameters to its notebooks and sets concurrency = 1. This serializes that pipeline's runs, not arbitrary manual notebook executions.

items.title: Freshness evidence
items.text:
The verifier evaluates these signals together:

  • setup_run_log
  • ag._watermarks
  • pipeline/notebook run history
  • Eventhouse max ingestion/event timestamps
  • Gold max source/event timestamps
  • generation timestamps and model/run IDs for ML output
  • alert/action state where deployed
Check Required? Operational meaning Setup run log Yes Historical setup completed and published a known run. Silver watermarks No Recent progress plus bounded receipt/inventory/sales consistency evidence. Eventhouse ingestion No Eventhouse has received recent optional events. Checkpoint identity No Recent Eventhouse extents can be tied to a stream and batch. Required model outputs Yes The six Reporting models were published by the required pipeline. Optional model outputs No Full-demo optional outputs are recent or have a valid empty snapshot. Experimental model outputs No Full-demo experimental outputs are recent or have a valid empty snapshot. Alerts No Optional alert queries are available and recent when rows exist.

items.title: Console severity versus report status
items.text:
Required failed/unknown checks are printed as errors and block deployment. Optional failures or unavailable evidence are warnings, not deployment errors. When all three optional streaming checks have no observed run evidence, the console groups them as an informational notice explaining that this is expected before stream-events is started. A partial stream or a network/permission failure is not classified as expected inactivity.

The report still records UNKNOWN and overall DEGRADED; no evidence is invented, marked passed, or silently skipped. Standalone verification retains its exit code 3 for optional degradation. The deployment command treats that as non-blocking and prints that required deployment is ready, while its journal retains DEGRADED. Actual optional workload failures remain named in the completion summary.

The persisted checks and freshness_lineage collections retain every structured record. Redaction and evidence-size limits apply inside each record, not to the number of checks; a truncation marker must never replace a check object. This keeps saved reports renderable and their check inventory consistent with the reported totals.

Required ML evidence selects the latest generated_at and a nonblank model_run_id from the same Gold row. Source/business dates remain separate lineage and cannot make an old model generation appear fresh. Setup and model evidence use a seven-day maximum age. Streaming watermark, Eventhouse ingestion, and checkpoint evidence use a 30-minute maximum age. Pipeline and data evidence must match the exact triggered run or the retained successful deployment-journal step. Historical full-demo execution is baseline evidence only; current repairs require new live verification.

Readiness correlates each model table with the pipeline that runs its producer. Notebooks 07 (market-basket mining) and 10 (promotion/elasticity) run inside ml-required to produce product_recommendations and price_elasticity. Their additional product_associations and promotion_lift outputs therefore use the ml-required freshness window, even though those outputs are optional or experimental. The remaining IMP-013 boundary includes a recent bounded stream that satisfies the three optional streaming checks, plus fresh changed-path readiness and cleanup/degradation validation.

items.title: Bounded streaming consistency
items.text:
The existing optional freshness.watermarks check calls adapter.data_consistency_signal() after checking watermark freshness. deploy/scripts/data_consistency.py owns the SQL; this does not add another taxonomy row or make streaming a required deployment capability.

  • Receipt and inventory shortcut-to-Silver key anti-joins sample ingestion timestamps from each source checkpoint minus 24 hours up to checkpoint minus three hours. The newest overlap is excluded for OneLake visibility.
  • Receipt identity uses receipt_id_ext; inventory identity uses trace_id.
  • Recent Silver inventory rows are checked for null balances, and receipts for missing store or non-null customer dimension keys. These integrity scans start at the respective window's lower bound; unlike the ingestion anti-joins, they do not exclude the newest three hours.
  • Gold sales_minute_store receipt counts and summed sales cents are compared by store with Silver receipts. The comparison uses interior complete hours, capped by both the settled receipt cutoff and Gold's latest timestamp; receipt counts must match and a cents difference greater than one is a mismatch.

Missing/invalid evidence or an empty receipt, inventory, or sales sample is UNKNOWN, not a zero-defect success. An observed positive mismatch is FAIL. Both degrade overall readiness because this streaming check is optional; other required failures still determine FAILED.

This is bounded receipt/inventory/sales sampling, not universal all-table or full-history integrity proof. tests/deploy/test_data_consistency.py executes equivalent SQL in SQLite and exercises the real adapter/runner path; live Fabric SQL execution and service consistency remain external gates.

items.title: Failure handling
items.text:
• Retain failed command, pipeline, and notebook run IDs.
  • Do not advance a checkpoint or watermark after failed required publication.
  • Do not overwrite healthy historical output before validating replacement output.
  • Distinguish required, optional, degraded, and manual-fallback results.
  • Preserve failed payloads or durable replay evidence.
  • Do not retry with --run-pipeline unless starting the setup pipeline is an intentional operator action.

Eventhouse micro-batches fail without checkpoint advancement, Silver replays merge by stable keys before watermark advancement, and setup attempts append durable status history. Historical and streaming publication stage and validate all candidate tables before promotion; partial promotion invokes compensating Delta restore/drop rollback. Deployment required-step outcomes persist in deploy/.generated/<env>/deploy-run.json; its readiness step links the separate bounded readiness report.

When a different run becomes latest, the previous deploy journal is first archived atomically at deploy/.generated/<env>/run-history/<hashed-run-id>.json. Inspect that history when comparing retries; do not overwrite evidence or hand-edit fingerprints to make legacy journals resumable.

Cleanup-only failure after successful promotion returns success with a warning. The setup freshness check retains cleanup_required evidence and the overall readiness result is DEGRADED, not FAILED, when no required check fails. Maintenance likewise distinguishes absent optional tables from real operation failures; the latter fail the notebook.

The setup-log row and remaining staging-table count are fetched in separate SQL statements. Fabric rejects combining distributed Lakehouse data with INFORMATION_SCHEMA catalog metadata in one query (SQL error 15816). Unavailable staging metadata remains UNKNOWN; it is not assumed to mean zero leftover tables.

Read-only readiness KQL requests retry KustoNetworkError up to three times, with five- and ten-second waits and a fresh client per attempt. Permission, query, and other service errors are not blindly retried. Exhausted reads remain errors, never empty success-shaped inventories. The four KQL inventory checks reuse one complete snapshot; if acquisition fails after retries, subsequent inventory checks remain UNKNOWN for that same run rather than mixing earlier failures with a later successful snapshot. Rerun read-only readiness after a persistent connection issue is resolved; do not rerun schema deployment or data generation solely to repeat these reads.

Cleanup readiness considers both the latest terminal setup status and remaining staging-table inventory. The SQL adapter counts tables in ag_stage, au_stage, and au_staging; a later successful Gold run cannot hide retained Silver staging artifacts merely by becoming the latest COMPLETED log row. Cleanup remains actionable until the leftovers are resolved.

Maintenance resolves fully qualified configured Lakehouse names. Only actual table absence is skippable; catalog, permission, and other real AnalysisException failures must not be treated as absent optional tables.

The exact-run recovery command accepts only explicitly named, recent, terminal-successful Fabric job IDs, verifies setup-to-ML dependency order, writes those IDs to the journal, and runs readiness before finalizing:

python -m deploy.scripts.adopt_pipeline_runs `
  --environment <env> `
  --run setup-pipeline=<job-id> `
  --run ml-required=<job-id>

Full-demo recovery also supplies ml-optional and ml-experimental.

items.title: Setup pipeline failed
items.text:
Inspect setup_run_log for the terminal state:

  • FAILED: staging/validation failed before final tables changed;
  • ROLLED_BACK: promotion failed and prior targets were restored;
  • ROLLBACK_FAILED: one or more targets could not be restored; preserve staging and repair from the logged target/version evidence;
  • COMPLETED_CLEANUP_FAILED or ROLLED_BACK_CLEANUP_FAILED: final data is promoted or restored correctly, but logged staging artifacts require cleanup.

Resume only after confirming the terminal state. Use a new run ID; duplicate run IDs are rejected.

Once the Silver watermark table has been initialized, the historical writer refuses replacement. Stop every writer and use a coordinated Silver/checkpoint reset for a deliberate rebuild; never delete only checkpoint or watermark state to bypass this guard.

items.title: KQL application failed
items.text: Inspect the generated database.kql, confirm the target database and operator permissions, then rerun the ordered script. Do not apply fragments out of order without recording the resulting state.

items.title: Streaming stopped or stale
items.text:
If streaming has never been started, DEGRADED results for watermarks, Eventhouse ingestion, and checkpoint identity are expected. Start a bounded stream only when the live-event story is required.

Check notebook errors, KQL permissions, resolved Query URI, ingestion failures, checkpoint path, persisted stream ID, Eventhouse shortcuts, and Silver watermarks. Restart with the same checkpoint root so the failed micro-batch retains its event identities and ingestion tags.

items.title: Ontology/task-flow binding missing
items.text: Run retail-setup post-ontology --env <env>. It creates the ontology when absent, rejects duplicates, republishes both agents, writes all selected task references, reads the graph back, and runs complete readiness.

items.title: Power BI table missing
items.text: Confirm whether the table exists in the Lakehouse. If it exists but SQL or Power BI cannot see it, run python -m deploy.scripts.refresh_sql_endpoint --environment <env>. If the table does not exist, run the owning setup/ML notebook or gate the dependent report page; do not create placeholder business data.

items.title: Destructive actions
items.text:
--recreate, Terraform destroy, and 99-reset-lakehouse require explicit target validation and confirmation. 99-reset-lakehouse is manual and is not orchestrated by normal pipelines.

Recreate polls for workspace-name absence after destroy. A timeout or repeated pagination marker fails the deploy before apply; do not bypass it with a fixed sleep.

items.title: CI platform coverage
items.text:
.github/workflows/tests.yml keeps the full sharded Spark and Parquet/E2E paths on Linux. Windows runs its non-Spark suite and discovers real Spark expression smoke tests with -m "spark and spark_no_filesystem". Current marked examples cover inventory replay/repair, delivery keyed as-of history, and truck lifecycle key pairing:

  • utility/tests/generation/test_streaming_inventory_runtime.py
  • utility/tests/generation/test_delivery_history_runtime.py
  • utility/tests/generation/test_streaming_truck_runtime.py

The Windows job provisions JDK 17 through the existing SHA-pinned actions/setup-java reference, sets TMPDIR to ${{ runner.temp }}, and uses SPARK_LOCAL_HOSTNAME=localhost. This is non-filesystem execution; missing Windows HADOOP_HOME/winutils still prevents the local Parquet/E2E path. Do not describe Windows as excluding every Spark test.

The recorded local results include passes for these three examples on Windows with the session's JDK 17. A separate generator selection passed 85 non-filesystem Spark tests; it is not the same selection as the representative Windows CI marker. The filename-discovery regression was fixed by marker selection, followed by 18 passing workflow/pipeline tests. The changed hosted workflow, full Spark suite, and live Delta/Fabric execution still require their own evidence.

items.title: Capacity
items.text: Start with a bounded store count and history window. Measure Spark duration, Eventhouse ingestion, storage, and report behavior before increasing capacity or enabling ML/ontology groups. Static runtime promises are not a contract.

items.title: Source and mode
items.text:
The Power BI Project (PBIP) at fabric/powerbi/retail_model.pbip versions the report and semantic model as source-controlled folders. The semantic model is Direct Lake over the target Lakehouse. Direct Lake reads OneLake tables directly without importing a second copy; the model is not a current KQL/DirectQuery hybrid.

Deployment rewrites the Direct Lake/OneLake binding to the target workspace and Lakehouse.

items.title: Active table set
items.text:
definition/model.tmdl currently contains 42 active table references. TMDL means Tabular Model Definition Language, the text format used to define the model:

  • 7 dimensions
  • 19 facts
  • 10 Gold aggregates
  • 6 ML tables

The six active ML tables are churn_predictions, customer_segments, demand_forecast, stockout_risk, product_recommendations, and price_elasticity. Two relationships bind product_recommendations.product_id and price_elasticity.product_id to dim_products.

The semantic-model source is the authority for active tables. The six ML tables are required Reporting outputs and have executable producer, schema, grain, temporal, lineage, intended-use, and limitation contracts in contracts/retail-demo.json.

items.title: Model design
items.text:
• Direct Lake source expression
  • explicit measures
  • discouraged implicit measures
  • date, geography, product, store, DC, and related hierarchies
  • relationships from dimensions to facts and aggregates
  • persona-oriented report pages

items.title: ML publication contract
items.text:
The historical generator remains valid without ML or Reporting. standard and full-demo publish infrastructure first, run setup-pipeline, and then wait for the exact ml-required run to finish. That pipeline runs the six required producers and 15-validate-required-ml-contract. A missing, empty, incompatible, duplicate, temporally incomplete, or invalid required output fails the run. Only terminal success permits the semantic model and report to be staged.

full-demo runs optional and experimental ML pipelines after Reporting is published. Failures in those isolated tiers leave required Reporting available and mark the deployment journal as degraded.

items.title: Deployment and validation
items.text:
The gated Reporting phase stages the semantic model and report under Reporting. During artifact staging, deployment sets every saved report date filter to the month containing end_date from utility/out/<env>/render-manifest.json. The checked-in PBIP remains a reusable template, while each deployed report opens on the latest period generated for that environment.

After setup and ML, deployment refreshes Lakehouse SQL endpoint metadata so new tables become visible to SQL and Power BI. A refresh failure is optional at the step level, but readiness still fails when a required model table cannot be queried.

Use scripts/configure_semantic_model.py only for supported manual workflows that need explicit workspace/Lakehouse binding.

Validation should confirm:

  1. All active tables exist.
  2. Direct Lake points to the intended Lakehouse.
  3. Required relationships and measures load.
  4. All six required ML tables pass their runtime contract.
  5. Access and field visibility match the intended persona.

Relevant tests:

  • tests/scripts/test_configure_semantic_model.py
  • tests/scripts/test_reference_integrity.py
  • tests/scripts/test_ml_semantic_contract_imp008.py
  • utility/tests/contracts/test_ml_contracts.py
  • utility/tests/generation/test_schema_contract.py

items.title: Identity contexts
items.text:
Context Identity Interactive deploy Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell operator Fabric REST and item deployment Operator-derived token/credential Fabric Terraform provider Azure CLI or explicit service-principal, OIDC, or managed identity; never Azure PowerShell session state KQL schema application Local deploy process with Eventhouse permissions Streaming notebook Fabric notebook runtime identity Ontology notebook Fabric notebook runtime identity; Power BI token exchanged for a Digital Operations workload token sent only to allowlisted Fabric HTTPS hosts Report/KQL/agent consumption Assigned Fabric/Power BI consumer identity

Every context must target the configured tenant, workspace, and data item.

items.title: Minimum roles
items.text:
Apply least privilege:

  • deployment operators need only the workspace/item permissions required to create or update selected assets;
  • streaming notebook identity needs KQL ingestion rights on the target database;
  • readers should receive Viewer/Database Viewer or narrower model access;
  • administrative roles should not be used for routine consumption.

Role assignments depend on tenant policy and deployment mode. Validate them in the target environment; an example command does not prove access.

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
Load secrets only from:

  • Azure sign-in;
  • GitHub Actions secrets;
  • environment variables;
  • Key Vault;
  • ignored local configuration.

Do not commit secrets to YAML, Terraform, notebooks, generated output, or docs. Do not replace bearer values with literal mask text in outgoing requests.

items.title: Data classification
items.text:
The supported dataset is generated synthetic data for demonstration only. Do not load production customer data into the demo.

Fabric workspace and item permissions are the default access boundary. The release does not require field masking, hashing, aggregation, or RLS for generated customer-like records.

items.title: Model and agent scope
items.text:
• The semantic model may expose generated customer-like fields to authorized workspace consumers.
  • Checked-in semantic-model RLS roles are not required.
  • Data Agent datasource instructions and user descriptions may remain unset in the default release. Persona-specific behavior remains optional under ENH-003.

The optional local app handles identity separately: its live embedding endpoint returns an operator-derived Power BI access token to the browser. Do not expose it as a shared authenticated service without separate hosting and delegated-identity controls. Approvals change local proposal records, not production systems; Eventhouse action logging is best-effort. See decision experience, THREAT-009, and SEC-012.

items.title: Documentation publication boundary
items.text: Public docs must not contain tenant IDs, workspace IDs, credentials, internal incident evidence, or generated local configuration. Canonical public content comes only from reviewed files in docs/.

items.title: Verification
items.text:
• request-level tests for bearer headers and target IDs;
  • secret scanning of source and generated output;
  • review of deployed workspace and item permissions;
  • Zensical output inspection for publication boundary.

items.title: Entry points
items.text:
• Windows: scripts/setup.ps1
  • macOS/Linux: scripts/setup.sh
  • Direct Python: python scripts/setup.py
  • Installed CLI: retail-setup

Both shell wrappers invoke the same Python guided setup. When --profile is omitted, both wrappers prepend --profile full-demo; a later explicit --profile argument overrides it. Direct scripts/setup.py and retail-setup commands use the same manifest-default full-demo profile.

Before dependencies are installed, scripts/solution_manifest.py reads the manifest version/hash, prerequisites, canonical examples, and profile names/default/publication expectations. scripts/setup.py derives its tool checks, profile choices, and profile default from that projection and validates its minimum Python version against the manifest and utility package constraint.

The guided bootstrap checks Git, Terraform, and Azure CLI, then installs the editable utility plus azure-identity, azure-kusto-data, fabric-cicd, mssql-python, and pyodbc. The lower-level deploy framework supports Azure PowerShell for Python Fabric clients only. Terraform still requires Azure CLI or a separately configured provider credential; alternatively, reuse validated outputs with --skip-terraform. The guided prerequisite check expects Azure CLI. On Windows and Linux, live Lakehouse freshness checks use mssql-python (Microsoft's Python SQL driver, installed automatically on non-macOS platforms) when Microsoft ODBC Driver 17 or 18 is not detected. On macOS, mssql-python is excluded because its supported wheel is not portable across the repository's macOS range; ODBC Driver 17 or 18 remains required.

items.title: Repeatable PowerShell environment preparation
items.text:
setup.ps1 resolves Conda from an existing CONDA_EXE/_CONDA_EXE file, native applications on PATH, or known installation paths. Command aliases and functions are not treated as executable paths: their Source can be the Conda module name rather than a filename. System Python discovery similarly selects native applications.

Conda activation uses the script emitted by <conda-executable> shell.powershell activate retail-demo, without loading the full shell hook or importing persistent Conda aliases/prompt functions. Listing, creation, and activation failures stop preparation explicitly. Installer output goes to the host, not the returned executable-path value. The existing finally restores the caller's process environment even after the Python setup exits unsuccessfully. tests/scripts/test_setup_powershell.py executes failed-then-successful launches in the same isolated PowerShell session and covers a stale Conda alias.

items.title: Windows Azure CLI broker recovery
items.text:
The bootstrap signs in to the configured tenant before starting deployment. It preserves Azure CLI's normal authentication method. On Windows only, a nonzero login result whose stderr contains incorrect storage parent or error code 2150171662 triggers exactly one browser-based retry with the child-process override AZURE_CORE_ENABLE_BROKER_ON_WINDOWS=false. That override also reaches the deployment child and its Azure CLI token requests. Neither the setup parent nor persisted CLI settings are changed.

Login stdin/stdout remain inherited; stderr is streamed immediately while retaining at most its final 8 KiB in memory for error classification. Dry runs start no login process. Azure PowerShell and non-Windows logins are unchanged. Other failures, cancellations, and policy denials remain terminal; failure of the browser retry stops before any deployment command. tests/scripts/test_setup_bootstrap.py covers the fallback, scope, interactive output, and fail-closed behavior.

items.title: configure
items.text:
retail-setup configure --workspace-name <name> --profile <profile> writes:

  • ignored deploy/config/environments/<env>.yml
  • ignored utility/config/environments/<env>.yaml

The environment key is derived from the normalized workspace name. A leading retail-demo- prefix is omitted, so workspace retail-demo-alice maps to environment alice. Reconfiguring another workspace creates another local overlay instead of changing shared defaults.

Generation settings are isolated by the same key. When that environment's generation file is absent, render reads legacy utility/config.yaml for compatibility; configure writes the environment-specific path.

Reconfiguring an existing environment removes the legacy spark.use_custom_pool and notebooks.include overlay keys. Deployment profiles now control both selections; unrelated Spark and notebook settings remain unchanged.

The active non-interactive inputs include:

  • tenant, workspace, capacity, Lakehouse, Eventhouse, and KQL database names;
  • authentication mode; the workspace name determines the environment;
  • store type: supercenter, grocery, hardware, or luxury;
  • history months, store count, and deterministic seed.

The CLI derives start_date and end_date from months with an end date of yesterday. The configuration model still accepts explicit dates for backward compatibility, but public examples use --months. core defaults to three months. Profiles with required ML/Reporting default to 18 months and reject windows shorter than 540 days because the required churn feature window, 90-day forward labels, and purged train/calibration/test partitions cannot be trained coherently on shorter history.

items.title: render
items.text:
retail-setup render --env <name> renders all notebooks in memory before writing any file. Unknown keys, missing values, or remaining tokens fail the operation without a partial notebook output set. It also writes utility/out/<env>/render-manifest.json with the resolved generation window. All twelve notebooks default to that environment directory. An explicit render output override is an advanced path; normal deployment consumes the environment-scoped output.

Notebook JSON is parsed structurally. Code substitutions are allowed only inside ordinary Python string literals, then encoded with Python literal representation and parsed for syntax; remaining tokens outside supported literals fail. Metadata is substituted as data and the notebook is serialized with JSON encoding. Quotes, backslashes, or statement-like text in --ref therefore remain string data rather than executable statements.

Without --ref, render requires Git metadata resolving the checkout's full commit revision. Missing Git metadata fails closed instead of falling back to mutable main. Setup 01 downloads dictionaries from GitHub at that revision, so it must exist on GitHub:

  • If HEAD is on a remote-tracking branch, render uses HEAD.
  • If HEAD isn't pushed, render uses the newest pushed ancestor and prints a note. This happens only when utility/data/dictionaries in the working tree, including uncommitted and untracked files, is identical to that ancestor.
  • Unpushed dictionary changes fail with a message to push or pass --ref.
  • A clone with no remote-tracking refs keeps HEAD.

An explicit --ref remains accepted; operators should use an immutable revision for reproducibility.

items.title: Dictionary source and cache
items.text:
Setup 01 owns Files/setup/dictionaries/_dictionary_manifest.json. An immutable 40- or 64-hex revision is reused only when manifest version, repository owner/name, ref, store type, complete expected JSON-file inventory, recorded optional absences, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes match. Mutable refs always refresh, even when the prior manifest matches.

All downloads and JSON validation complete in staging before publication. Only a 404 for a declared optional file is accepted; other download/JSON failures stop the attempt. Publication invalidates the old manifest, replaces files, removes stale optional files, and atomically publishes the new manifest last. This is not an atomic directory swap or distributed transaction: interrupted publication cannot leave a manifest that marks partial data as valid. utility/tests/test_dictionary_seed_cache.py covers revision changes, corruption, interrupted downloads, immutable hits, mutable refresh, optional 404 behavior, and invalid JSON.

Fork execution must set RETAIL_SETUP_REPOSITORY_OWNER and RETAIL_SETUP_REPOSITORY_NAME in the notebook runtime environment. Defaults are amattas and retail-demo. The CLI injects the ref but does not auto-detect a fork or automatically forward local environment overrides to Fabric. A fork-only commit must be fetched from the repository that owns it.

The wheel includes dictionaries and all twelve notebook resources under retail_setup/resources/; loaders/rendering can use these outside a checkout. utility/pyproject.toml pins the build backend to hatchling==1.27.0. After generator/template work finishes, rebuild generated notebooks before claiming the packaged/rendered artifact set is current.

items.text:
1. setup-01-seed-dictionaries.ipynb
  2. setup-02-generate-dimensions.ipynb
